def create_sample_client():
    """Create a sample client for testing the online prediction service."""
    
    class PredictionClient:
        """Client for interacting with online prediction service."""
        
        def __init__(self, base_url: str = "http://localhost:5000"):
            self.base_url = base_url
            self.session = None
        
        async def __aenter__(self):
            self.session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
            return self
        
        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
            if self.session:
                await self
```python
                await self.session.close()
        
        async def predict(self, data: List[float], request_id: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Send prediction request."""
            payload = {'data': data}
            if request_id:
                payload['request_id'] = request_id
            
            async with self.session.post(f"{self.base_url}/predict", json=payload) as response:
                if response.status == 200:
                    return await response.json()
                else:
                    raise Exception(f"Prediction failed: {response.status}")
        
        async def predict_batch(self, batch_data: List[List[float]], 
                               request_ids: List[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Send batch prediction request."""
            payload = {'data': batch_data}
            if request_ids:
                payload['request_ids'] = request_ids
            
            async with self.session.post(f"{self.base_url}/predict/batch", json=payload) as response:
                if response.status == 200:
                    return await response.json()
                else:
                    raise Exception(f"Batch prediction failed: {response.status}")
        
        async def predict_async(self, data: List[float], callback_url: str = None) -> str:
            """Send async prediction request."""
            payload = {'data': data}
            if callback_url:
                payload['callback_url'] = callback_url
            
            async with self.session.post(f"{self.base_url}/predict/async", json=payload) as response:
                if response.status == 200:
                    result = await response.json()
                    return result['request_id']
                else:
                    raise Exception(f"Async prediction failed: {response.status}")
        
        async def get_health(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Get service health status."""
            async with self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}/health") as response:
                return await response.json()
        
        async def get_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Get service statistics."""
            async with self.session.get(f"{self.base_url}/stats") as response:
                return await response.json()
        
        async def update_model(self, model_path: str, model_id: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Update service model."""
            payload = {'model_path': model_path}
            if model_id:
                payload['model_id'] = model_id
            
            async with self.session.post(f"{self.base_url}/model", json=payload) as response:
                return await response.json()
        
        async def benchmark(self, num_requests: int = 100, concurrent: int = 10) -> Dict[str, Any]:
            """Benchmark the prediction service."""
            import time
            import random
            
            # Generate test data
            test_data = [[random.random() for _ in range(784)] for _ in range(num_requests)]
            
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Send concurrent requests
            semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrent)
            
            async def single_request(data):
                async with semaphore:
                    try:
                        return await self.predict(data)
                    except Exception as e:
                        return {'error': str(e)}
            
            # Execute all requests
            tasks = [single_request(data) for data in test_data]
            results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
            
            end_time = time.time()
            
            # Analyze results
            successful = len([r for r in results if 'error' not in r])
            failed = len([r for r in results if 'error' in r])
            total_time = end_time - start_time
            
            return {
                'total_requests': num_requests,
                'successful': successful,
                'failed': failed,
                'total_time': total_time,
                'requests_per_second': num_requests / total_time,
                'success_rate': successful / num_requests
            }
    
    return PredictionClient

def create_sample_model():
    """Create and save a sample model for testing."""
    # Create simple model
    model = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(784, 256),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(256, 128),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(128, 10)
    )
    
    # Save model
    torch.save(model.state_dict(), "online_model.pt")
    
    # Create TorchScript version
    model.eval()
    example_input = torch.randn(1, 784)
    traced_model = torch.jit.trace(model, example_input)
    traced_model.save("online_traced_model.pt")
    
    logger.info("Sample models created: online_model.pt, online_traced_model.pt")
    return "online_traced_model.pt"

async def run_load_test():
    """Run a comprehensive load test."""
    print("=== Running Load Test ===")
    
    client_class = create_sample_client()
    
    async with client_class() as client:
        # Test different load levels
        load_levels = [
            {'requests': 10, 'concurrent': 1},
            {'requests': 50, 'concurrent': 5},
            {'requests': 100, 'concurrent': 10},
            {'requests': 200, 'concurrent': 20}
        ]
        
        for load in load_levels:
            print(f"\nTesting {load['requests']} requests with {load['concurrent']} concurrent...")
            
            try:
                result = await client.benchmark(
                    num_requests=load['requests'],
                    concurrent=load['concurrent']
                )
                
                print(f"  Success rate: {result['success_rate']:.2%}")
                print(f"  Requests/sec: {result['requests_per_second']:.1f}")
                print(f"  Total time: {result['total_time']:.2f}s")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  Load test failed: {e}")

## 194. A/B Testing Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import json
import hashlib
import time
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional, Tuple
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from enum import Enum
import sqlite3
import threading
from collections import defaultdict
import scipy.stats as stats
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class ExperimentStatus(Enum):
    """Experiment status enumeration."""
    DRAFT = "draft"
    RUNNING = "running"
    PAUSED = "paused"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"

@dataclass
class ExperimentConfig:
    """Configuration for A/B test experiment."""
    experiment_id: str
    name: str
    description: str
    model_a_path: str
    model_b_path: str
    traffic_split: float = 0.5  # Fraction of traffic to model B
    start_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    end_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    min_sample_size: int = 1000
    significance_level: float = 0.05
    metrics: List[str] = None
    user_groups: List[str] = None
    status: ExperimentStatus = ExperimentStatus.DRAFT

@dataclass
class ExperimentResult:
    """Result from A/B test prediction."""
    experiment_id: str
    user_id: str
    model_variant: str  # 'A' or 'B'
    prediction: Any
    confidence: float
    response_time: float
    timestamp: datetime
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = None

@dataclass
class MetricResult:
    """Statistical result for a metric."""
    metric_name: str
    model_a_value: float
    model_b_value: float
    p_value: float
    confidence_interval: Tuple[float, float]
    effect_size: float
    is_significant: bool
    sample_size_a: int
    sample_size_b: int

class TrafficSplitter:
    """Handles traffic splitting for A/B testing."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.hash_cache = {}
    
    def assign_variant(self, user_id: str, traffic_split: float, 
                      experiment_id: str) -> str:
        """
        Assign user to variant based on consistent hashing.
        
        Args:
            user_id: Unique user identifier
            traffic_split: Fraction of traffic for variant B
            experiment_id: Experiment identifier for consistent assignment
            
        Returns:
            'A' or 'B' variant assignment
        """
        # Create hash key
        hash_key = f"{experiment_id}:{user_id}"
        
        # Check cache first
        if hash_key in self.hash_cache:
            hash_value = self.hash_cache[hash_key]
        else:
            # Generate consistent hash
            hash_value = int(hashlib.md5(hash_key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16)
            self.hash_cache[hash_key] = hash_value
        
        # Convert to probability
        probability = (hash_value % 10000) / 10000.0
        
        # Assign variant
        return 'B' if probability < traffic_split else 'A'
    
    def get_assignment_probability(self, user_id: str, experiment_id: str) -> float:
        """Get the probability hash for a user."""
        hash_key = f"{experiment_id}:{user_id}"
        hash_value = int(hashlib.md5(hash_key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16)
        return (hash_value % 10000) / 10000.0

class ExperimentTracker:
    """Tracks experiment results and metrics."""
    
    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "ab_experiments.db"):
        self.db_path = db_path
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self._init_database()
    
    def _init_database(self):
        """Initialize SQLite database for experiment tracking."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiments (
                    experiment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    config TEXT,
                    status TEXT,
                    created_at TIMESTAMP,
                    updated_at TIMESTAMP
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiment_results (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    experiment_id TEXT,
                    user_id TEXT,
                    model_variant TEXT,
                    prediction TEXT,
                    confidence REAL,
                    response_time REAL,
                    timestamp TIMESTAMP,
                    metadata TEXT,
                    FOREIGN KEY (experiment_id) REFERENCES experiments (experiment_id)
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiment_metrics (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    experiment_id TEXT,
                    metric_name TEXT,
                    model_variant TEXT,
                    metric_value REAL,
                    timestamp TIMESTAMP,
                    FOREIGN KEY (experiment_id) REFERENCES experiments (experiment_id)
                )
            """)
            
            conn.commit()
    
    def create_experiment(self, config: ExperimentConfig):
        """Create new experiment."""
        with self.lock:
            with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
                conn.execute("""
                    INSERT OR REPLACE INTO experiments 
                    (experiment_id, config, status, created_at, updated_at)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                """, (
                    config.experiment_id,
                    json.dumps(asdict(config), default=str),
                    config.status.value,
                    datetime.now(),
                    datetime.now()
                ))
                conn.commit()
        
        logger.info(f"Created experiment: {config.experiment_id}")
    
    def update_experiment_status(self, experiment_id: str, status: ExperimentStatus):
        """Update experiment status."""
        with self.lock:
            with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
                conn.execute("""
                    UPDATE experiments 
                    SET status = ?, updated_at = ?
                    WHERE experiment_id = ?
                """, (status.value, datetime.now(), experiment_id))
                conn.commit()
        
        logger.info(f"Updated experiment {experiment_id} status to {status.value}")
    
    def log_result(self, result: ExperimentResult):
        """Log experiment result."""
        with self.lock:
            with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
                conn.execute("""
                    INSERT INTO experiment_results 
                    (experiment_id, user_id, model_variant, prediction, confidence, 
                     response_time, timestamp, metadata)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                """, (
                    result.experiment_id,
                    result.user_id,
                    result.model_variant,
                    json.dumps(result.prediction),
                    result.confidence,
                    result.response_time,
                    result.timestamp,
                    json.dumps(result.metadata or {})
                ))
                conn.commit()
    
    def log_metric(self, experiment_id: str, metric_name: str, 
                  model_variant: str, metric_value: float):
        """Log custom metric."""
        with self.lock:
            with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
                conn.execute("""
                    INSERT INTO experiment_metrics 
                    (experiment_id, metric_name, model_variant, metric_value, timestamp)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                """, (experiment_id, metric_name, model_variant, metric_value, datetime.now()))
                conn.commit()
    
    def get_experiment_results(self, experiment_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Get all results for an experiment."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            return pd.read_sql_query("""
                SELECT * FROM experiment_results 
                WHERE experiment_id = ?
                ORDER BY timestamp
            """, conn, params=(experiment_id,))
    
    def get_experiment_metrics(self, experiment_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Get all metrics for an experiment."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            return pd.read_sql_query("""
                SELECT * FROM experiment_metrics 
                WHERE experiment_id = ?
                ORDER BY timestamp
            """, conn, params=(experiment_id,))

class StatisticalAnalyzer:
    """Performs statistical analysis of A/B test results."""
    
    def __init__(self, significance_level: float = 0.05):
        self.significance_level = significance_level
    
    def analyze_metric(self, values_a: List[float], values_b: List[float], 
                      metric_name: str) -> MetricResult:
        """
        Perform statistical analysis on a metric.
        
        Args:
            values_a: Metric values for variant A
            values_b: Metric values for variant B
            metric_name: Name of the metric being analyzed
            
        Returns:
            Statistical analysis results
        """
        if len(values_a) == 0 or len(values_b) == 0:
            return MetricResult(
                metric_name=metric_name,
                model_a_value=0.0,
                model_b_value=0.0,
                p_value=1.0,
                confidence_interval=(0.0, 0.0),
                effect_size=0.0,
                is_significant=False,
                sample_size_a=len(values_a),
                sample_size_b=len(values_b)
            )
        
        # Calculate basic statistics
        mean_a = np.mean(values_a)
        mean_b = np.mean(values_b)
        
        # Perform t-test
        t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(values_a, values_b)
        
        # Calculate effect size (Cohen's d)
        pooled_std = np.sqrt(((len(values_a) - 1) * np.var(values_a, ddof=1) + 
                             (len(values_b) - 1) * np.var(values_b, ddof=1)) / 
                            (len(values_a) + len(values_b) - 2))
        
        effect_size = (mean_b - mean_a) / pooled_std if pooled_std > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Calculate confidence interval for difference
        se_diff = pooled_std * np.sqrt(1/len(values_a) + 1/len(values_b))
        df = len(values_a) + len(values_b) - 2
        t_critical = stats.t.ppf(1 - self.significance_level/2, df)
        
        diff = mean_b - mean_a
        margin_error = t_critical * se_diff
        confidence_interval = (diff - margin_error, diff + margin_error)
        
        return MetricResult(
            metric_name=metric_name,
            model_a_value=mean_a,
            model_b_value=mean_b,
            p_value=p_value,
            confidence_interval=confidence_interval,
            effect_size=effect_size,
            is_significant=p_value < self.significance_level,
            sample_size_a=len(values_a),
            sample_size_b=len(values_b)
        )
    
    def analyze_conversion_rate(self, conversions_a: List[bool], 
                               conversions_b: List[bool]) -> MetricResult:
        """Analyze conversion rate using proportion test."""
        count_a = sum(conversions_a)
        count_b = sum(conversions_b)
        n_a = len(conversions_a)
        n_b = len(conversions_b)
        
        if n_a == 0 or n_b == 0:
            return MetricResult(
                metric_name="conversion_rate",
                model_a_value=0.0,
                model_b_value=0.0,
                p_value=1.0,
                confidence_interval=(0.0, 0.0),
                effect_size=0.0,
                is_significant=False,
                sample_size_a=n_a,
                sample_size_b=n_b
            )
        
        rate_a = count_a / n_a
        rate_b = count_b / n_b
        
        # Two-proportion z-test
        pooled_rate = (count_a + count_b) / (n_a + n_b)
        se = np.sqrt(pooled_rate * (1 - pooled_rate) * (1/n_a + 1/n_b))
        
        if se > 0:
            z_stat = (rate_b - rate_a) / se
            p_value = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z_stat)))
        else:
            z_stat = 0
            p_value = 1.0
        
        # Effect size for proportions
        effect_size = (rate_b - rate_a) / np.sqrt(pooled_rate * (1 - pooled_rate))
        
        # Confidence interval for difference in proportions
        se_diff = np.sqrt(rate_a * (1 - rate_a) / n_a + rate_b * (1 - rate_b) / n_b)
        z_critical = stats.norm.ppf(1 - self.significance_level/2)
        
        diff = rate_b - rate_a
        margin_error = z_critical * se_diff
        confidence_interval = (diff - margin_error, diff + margin_error)
        
        return MetricResult(
            metric_name="conversion_rate",
            model_a_value=rate_a,
            model_b_value=rate_b,
            p_value=p_value,
            confidence_interval=confidence_interval,
            effect_size=effect_size,
            is_significant=p_value < self.significance_level,
            sample_size_a=n_a,
            sample_size_b=n_b
        )
    
    def calculate_sample_size(self, baseline_rate: float, minimum_detectable_effect: float,
                             power: float = 0.8) -> int:
        """Calculate required sample size for experiment."""
        alpha = self.significance_level
        beta = 1 - power
        
        # For proportion test
        p1 = baseline_rate
        p2 = baseline_rate * (1 + minimum_detectable_effect)
        
        pooled_p = (p1 + p2) / 2
        
        z_alpha = stats.norm.ppf(1 - alpha/2)
        z_beta = stats.norm.ppf(power)
        
        numerator = (z_alpha * np.sqrt(2 * pooled_p * (1 - pooled_p)) + 
                    z_beta * np.sqrt(p1 * (1 - p1) + p2 * (1 - p2))) ** 2
        
        denominator = (p2 - p1) ** 2
        
        return int(np.ceil(numerator / denominator))

class ABTestPredictor:
    """Main A/B testing predictor that manages experiments."""
    
    def __init__(self, device: str = 'cpu'):
        self.device = torch.device(device)
        self.experiments = {}  # experiment_id -> config
        self.models = {}  # model_path -> loaded model
        self.splitter = TrafficSplitter()
        self.tracker = ExperimentTracker()
        self.analyzer = StatisticalAnalyzer()
        
        # Performance tracking
        self.prediction_stats = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    
    def _load_model(self, model_path: str) -> nn.Module:
        """Load model from path with caching."""
        if model_path in self.models:
            return self.models[model_path]
        
        # Load model based on file extension
        if model_path.endswith('.pt') and 'traced' in model_path:
            model = torch.jit.load(model_path, map_location=self.device)
        else:
            # For demo purposes, create a simple model
            model = self._create_demo_model()
            if model_path.endswith('.pt'):
                try:
                    state_dict = torch.load(model_path, map_location=self.device)
                    model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
                except:
                    logger.warning(f"Could not load state dict from {model_path}, using random weights")
        
        model.eval()
        model.to(self.device)
        self.models[model_path] = model
        
        logger.info(f"Loaded model: {model_path}")
        return model
    
    def _create_demo_model(self) -> nn.Module:
        """Create demo model for testing."""
        return nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(784, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )
    
    def create_experiment(self, config: ExperimentConfig):
        """Create and register new A/B test experiment."""
        # Validate configuration
        if config.traffic_split < 0 or config.traffic_split > 1:
            raise ValueError("Traffic split must be between 0 and 1")
        
        if config.min_sample_size < 10:
            raise ValueError("Minimum sample size must be at least 10")
        
        # Load both models to validate they exist
        self._load_model(config.model_a_path)
        self._load_model(config.model_b_path)
        
        # Store experiment configuration
        self.experiments[config.experiment_id] = config
        
        # Save to database
        self.tracker.create_experiment(config)
        
        logger.info(f"Created A/B test experiment: {config.experiment_id}")
    
    def start_experiment(self, experiment_id: str):
        """Start an experiment."""
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        config.status = ExperimentStatus.RUNNING
        config.start_time = datetime.now()
        
        self.tracker.update_experiment_status(experiment_id, ExperimentStatus.RUNNING)
        logger.info(f"Started experiment: {experiment_id}")
    
    def stop_experiment(self, experiment_id: str):
        """Stop an experiment."""
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        config.status = ExperimentStatus.COMPLETED
        config.end_time = datetime.now()
        
        self.tracker.update_experiment_status(experiment_id, ExperimentStatus.COMPLETED)
        logger.info(f"Stopped experiment: {experiment_id}")
    
    def predict(self, data: np.ndarray, user_id: str, 
                experiment_id: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Make prediction with A/B testing.
        
        Args:
            data: Input data for prediction
            user_id: Unique user identifier
            experiment_id: Specific experiment to use (optional)
            
        Returns:
            Prediction result with experiment metadata
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # If no experiment specified, use the first running experiment
        if experiment_id is None:
            running_experiments = [
                exp_id for exp_id, config in self.experiments.items()
                if config.status == ExperimentStatus.RUNNING
            ]
            if not running_experiments:
                raise ValueError("No running experiments found")
            experiment_id = running_experiments[0]
        
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        
        # Check if experiment is running
        if config.status != ExperimentStatus.RUNNING:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} is not running")
        
        # Assign user to variant
        variant = self.splitter.assign_variant(
            user_id, config.traffic_split, experiment_id
        )
        
        # Select model based on variant
        model_path = config.model_a_path if variant == 'A' else config.model_b_path
        model = self._load_model(model_path)
        
        # Preprocess data
        if isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
            tensor_data = torch.tensor(data, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        else:
            tensor_data = torch.tensor(np.array(data), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        
        if len(tensor_data.shape) == 1:
            tensor_data = tensor_data.unsqueeze(0)
        
        # Make prediction
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits = model(tensor_data)
            probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
            confidence, prediction = torch.max(probabilities, dim=1)
        
        processing_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Create result
        result = ExperimentResult(
            experiment_id=experiment_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            model_variant=variant,
            prediction=prediction.item(),
            confidence=confidence.item(),
            response_time=processing_time,
            timestamp=datetime.now(),
            metadata={
                'model_path': model_path,
                'traffic_split': config.traffic_split
            }
        )
        
        # Log result
        self.tracker.log_result(result)
        
        # Update stats
        self.prediction_stats[experiment_id][variant] += 1
        
        return {
            'prediction': result.prediction,
            'confidence': result.confidence,
            'variant': variant,
            'experiment_id': experiment_id,
            'response_time': processing_time
        }
    
    def log_custom_metric(self, experiment_id: str, user_id: str, 
                         metric_name: str, metric_value: float):
        """Log custom metric for A/B test analysis."""
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        # Get user's variant assignment
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        variant = self.splitter.assign_variant(
            user_id, config.traffic_split, experiment_id
        )
        
        # Log metric
        self.tracker.log_metric(experiment_id, metric_name, variant, metric_value)
    
    def analyze_experiment(self, experiment_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Perform comprehensive analysis of experiment results."""
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        
        # Get experiment data
        results_df = self.tracker.get_experiment_results(experiment_id)
        metrics_df = self.tracker.get_experiment_metrics(experiment_id)
        
        if len(results_df) == 0:
            return {
                'experiment_id': experiment_id,
                'status': 'no_data',
                'message': 'No data available for analysis'
            }
        
        analysis = {
            'experiment_id': experiment_id,
            'config': asdict(config),
            'sample_sizes': {
                'total': len(results_df),
                'variant_a': len(results_df[results_df['model_variant'] == 'A']),
                'variant_b': len(results_df[results_df['model_variant'] == 'B'])
            },
            'metrics': {}
        }
        
        # Analyze basic metrics from prediction results
        for metric in ['confidence', 'response_time']:
            values_a = results_df[results_df['model_variant'] == 'A'][metric].values
            values_b = results_df[results_df['model_variant'] == 'B'][metric].values
            
            metric_result = self.analyzer.analyze_metric(values_a, values_b, metric)
            analysis['metrics'][metric] = asdict(metric_result)
        
        # Analyze custom metrics if available
        if len(metrics_df) > 0:
            for metric_name in metrics_df['metric_name'].unique():
                metric_data = metrics_df[metrics_df['metric_name'] == metric_name]
                
                values_a = metric_data[metric_data['model_variant'] == 'A']['metric_value'].values
                values_b = metric_data[metric_data['model_variant'] == 'B']['metric_value'].values
                
                metric_result = self.analyzer.analyze_metric(values_a, values_b, metric_name)
                analysis['metrics'][metric_name] = asdict(metric_result)
        
        # Calculate statistical power and recommendations
        analysis['recommendations'] = self._generate_recommendations(analysis, config)
        
        return analysis
    
    def _generate_recommendations(self, analysis: Dict[str, Any], 
                                 config: ExperimentConfig) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate recommendations based on analysis results."""
        recommendations = {
            'continue_experiment': True,
            'reasons': [],
            'suggested_actions': []
        }
        
        total_samples = analysis['sample_sizes']['total']
        min_samples = config.min_sample_size
        
        # Check sample size
        if total_samples < min_samples:
            recommendations['continue_experiment'] = True
            recommendations['reasons'].append(
                f"Sample size ({total_samples}) below minimum ({min_samples})"
            )
            recommendations['suggested_actions'].append(
                f"Continue experiment until {min_samples} samples collected"
            )
        
        # Check for significant results
        significant_metrics = []
        for metric_name, metric_data in analysis['metrics'].items():
            if metric_data['is_significant']:
                significant_metrics.append(metric_name)
        
        if significant_metrics:
            recommendations['continue_experiment'] = False
            recommendations['reasons'].append(
                f"Significant results found for: {', '.join(significant_metrics)}"
            )
            recommendations['suggested_actions'].append(
                "Consider stopping experiment and implementing winning variant"
            )
        
        # Check for balance in variant assignment
        variant_a_ratio = analysis['sample_sizes']['variant_a'] / total_samples
        expected_ratio = 1 - config.traffic_split
        
        if abs(variant_a_ratio - expected_ratio) > 0.1:  # 10% tolerance
            recommendations['suggested_actions'].append(
                f"Traffic split imbalance detected. Expected {expected_ratio:.1%} for A, "
                f"got {variant_a_ratio:.1%}"
            )
        
        return recommendations
    
    def get_experiment_summary(self, experiment_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get real-time experiment summary."""
        if experiment_id not in self.experiments:
            raise ValueError(f"Experiment {experiment_id} not found")
        
        config = self.experiments[experiment_id]
        results_df = self.tracker.get_experiment_results(experiment_id)
        
        summary = {
            'experiment_id': experiment_id,
            'name': config.name,
            'status': config.status.value,
            'start_time': config.start_time.isoformat() if config.start_time else None,
            'duration_hours': None,
            'total_predictions': len(results_df),
            'variant_distribution': {},
            'recent_metrics': {}
        }
        
        if config.start_time:
            duration = datetime.now() - config.start_time
            summary['duration_hours'] = duration.total_seconds() / 3600
        
        if len(results_df) > 0:
            # Variant distribution
            variant_counts = results_df['model_variant'].value_counts()
            total_count = len(results_df)
            
            summary['variant_distribution'] = {
                'A': {
                    'count': variant_counts.get('A', 0),
                    'percentage': variant_counts.get('A', 0) / total_count * 100
                },
                'B': {
                    'count': variant_counts.get('B', 0),
                    'percentage': variant_counts.get('B', 0) / total_count * 100
                }
            }
            
            # Recent performance (last hour)
            recent_cutoff = datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
            recent_results = results_df[
                pd.to_datetime(results_df['timestamp']) > recent_cutoff
            ]
            
            if len(recent_results) > 0:
                for variant in ['A', 'B']:
                    variant_data = recent_results[recent_results['model_variant'] == variant]
                    if len(variant_data) > 0:
                        summary['recent_metrics'][f'variant_{variant}'] = {
                            'predictions': len(variant_data),
                            'avg_confidence': variant_data['confidence'].mean(),
                            'avg_response_time': variant_data['response_time'].mean()
                        }
        
        return summary
    
    def get_active_experiments(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get list of all active experiments."""
        active = []
        
        for exp_id, config in self.experiments.items():
            if config.status == ExperimentStatus.RUNNING:
                summary = self.get_experiment_summary(exp_id)
                active.append(summary)
        
        return active

    def save_dashboard(self, filename: str = "ab_test_dashboard.html"):

def create_sample_models():
    """Create sample models for A/B testing."""
    
    # Model A - Baseline
    model_a = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(784, 256),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Dropout(0.2),
        nn.Linear(256, 128),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(128, 10)
    )
    
    # Model B - Improved (different architecture)
    model_b = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(784, 512),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.BatchNorm1d(512),
        nn.Dropout(0.3),
        nn.Linear(512, 256),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.BatchNorm1d(256),
        nn.Dropout(0.2),
        nn.Linear(256, 128),
        nn.ReLU(),
        nn.Linear(128, 10)
    )
    
    # Save models
    torch.save(model_a.state_dict(), "model_a.pt")
    torch.save(model_b.state_dict(), "model_b.pt")
    
    # Create TorchScript versions
    model_a.eval()
    model_b.eval()
    
    example_input = torch.randn(1, 784)
    
    traced_a = torch.jit.trace(model_a, example_input)
    traced_b = torch.jit.trace(model_b, example_input)
    
    traced_a.save("model_a_traced.pt")
    traced_b.save("model_b_traced.pt")
    
    logger.info("Sample models created: model_a.pt, model_b.pt, model_a_traced.pt, model_b_traced.pt")
    return "model_a_traced.pt", "model_b_traced.pt"

def run_ab_test_simulation():
    """Run a complete A/B test simulation."""
    
    print("=== A/B Test Simulation ===")
    
    # Create sample models
    model_a_path, model_b_path = create_sample_models()
    
    # Initialize predictor
    predictor = ABTestPredictor()
    
    # Create experiment configuration
    config = ExperimentConfig(
        experiment_id="accuracy_test_001",
        name="Model Accuracy Comparison",
        description="Testing improved model against baseline",
        model_a_path=model_a_path,
        model_b_path=model_b_path,
        traffic_split=0.5,
        min_sample_size=200,
        significance_level=0.05,
        metrics=["accuracy", "confidence", "response_time"]
    )
    
    # Create and start experiment
    predictor.create_experiment(config)
    predictor.start_experiment(config.experiment_id)
    
    print(f"Started experiment: {config.name}")
    
    # Simulate users making predictions
    users = [f"user_{i}" for i in range(100)]
    
    print("\nSimulating predictions...")
    for i in range(500):
        user_id = np.random.choice(users)
        test_data = np.random.randn(784)
        
        try:
            result = predictor.predict(test_data, user_id, config.experiment_id)
            
            # Simulate custom metrics
            if np.random.random() < 0.7:  # 70% accuracy rate
                predictor.log_custom_metric(
                    config.experiment_id, user_id, "accuracy", 1.0
                )
            else:
                predictor.log_custom_metric(
                    config.experiment_id, user_id, "accuracy", 0.0
                )
            
            # Simulate user satisfaction (variant B is slightly better)
            satisfaction_score = 4.0 + np.random.normal(0, 0.5)
            if result['variant'] == 'B':
                satisfaction_score += 0.3  # B is better
            
            predictor.log_custom_metric(
                config.experiment_id, user_id, "satisfaction", 
                max(1.0, min(5.0, satisfaction_score))
            )
            
            if (i + 1) % 100 == 0:
                print(f"  Completed {i + 1} predictions")
        
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  Error in prediction {i}: {e}")
    
    # Analyze results
    print("\nAnalyzing experiment results...")
    analysis = predictor.analyze_experiment(config.experiment_id)
    
    print(f"\nExperiment Analysis:")
    print(f"Total samples: {analysis['sample_sizes']['total']}")
    print(f"Variant A samples: {analysis['sample_sizes']['variant_a']}")
    print(f"Variant B samples: {analysis['sample_sizes']['variant_b']}")
    
    print(f"\nMetric Results:")
    for metric_name, metric_data in analysis['metrics'].items():
        print(f"\n{metric_name.upper()}:")
        print(f"  Variant A: {metric_data['model_a_value']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Variant B: {metric_data['model_b_value']:.4f}")
        print(f"  P-value: {metric_data['p_value']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Significant: {metric_data['is_significant']}")
        print(f"  Effect size: {metric_data['effect_size']:.4f}")
    
    print(f"\nRecommendations:")
    for reason in analysis['recommendations']['reasons']:
        print(f"  - {reason}")
    for action in analysis['recommendations']['suggested_actions']:
        print(f"  - {action}")
    
    # Stop experiment
    predictor.stop_experiment(config.experiment_id)
    
    # Get final summary
    summary = predictor.get_experiment_summary(config.experiment_id)
    print(f"\nFinal Summary:")
    print(f"Status: {summary['status']}")
    print(f"Duration: {summary['duration_hours']:.2f} hours")
    print(f"Total predictions: {summary['total_predictions']}")
    
    return predictor, analysis

if __name__ == "__main__":

## 195. Canary Deployment Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np
import time
import logging
import threading
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, asdict
from enum import Enum
import json
import sqlite3
from collections import deque, defaultdict
import psutil
import requests
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import asyncio
import aiohttp

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class DeploymentStatus(Enum):
    """Canary deployment status."""
    PREPARING = "preparing"
    CANARY_ACTIVE = "canary_active"
    PROMOTING = "promoting"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    ROLLING_BACK = "rolling_back"
    FAILED = "failed"

@dataclass
class CanaryConfig:
    """Configuration for canary deployment."""
    deployment_id: str
    name: str
    stable_model_path: str
    canary_model_path: str
    initial_traffic_percentage: float = 5.0
    max_traffic_percentage: float = 100.0
    traffic_increment: float = 10.0
    promotion_interval_minutes: int = 30
    success_criteria: Dict[str, Any] = None
    rollback_criteria: Dict[str, Any] = None
    max_duration_hours: int = 24

@dataclass
class HealthMetrics:
    """Health metrics for deployment monitoring."""
    timestamp: datetime
    model_version: str
    request_count: int
    error_count: int
    avg_response_time: float
    avg_confidence: float
    cpu_usage: float
    memory_usage: float
    custom_metrics: Dict[str, float] = None

class HealthMonitor:
    """Monitors health metrics for canary deployments."""
    
    def __init__(self, window_size_minutes: int = 10):
        self.window_size = timedelta(minutes=window_size_minutes)
        self.metrics_history = deque()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        
        # Real-time metrics tracking
        self.current_metrics = {
            'stable': defaultdict(list),
            'canary': defaultdict(list)
        }
        
    def record_request(self, model_version: str, response_time: float, 
                      confidence: float, error: bool = False):
        """Record individual request metrics."""
        with self.lock:
            timestamp = datetime.now()
            
            self.current_metrics[model_version]['response_times'].append(response_time)
            self.current_metrics[model_version]['confidences'].append(confidence)
            self.current_metrics[model_version]['requests'].append(timestamp)
            
            if error:
                self.current_metrics[model_version]['errors'].append(timestamp)
    
    def record_system_metrics(self, model_version: str):
        """Record system-level metrics."""
        with self.lock:
            cpu_usage = psutil.cpu_percent()
            memory_usage = psutil.virtual_memory().percent
            
            metrics = HealthMetrics(
                timestamp=datetime.now(),
                model_version=model_version,
                request_count=len(self.current_metrics[model_version]['requests']),
                error_count=len(self.current_metrics[model_version]['errors']),
                avg_response_time=np.mean(self.current_metrics[model_version]['response_times']) 
                                 if self.current_metrics[model_version]['response_times'] else 0.0,
                avg_confidence=np.mean(self.current_metrics[model_version]['confidences']) 
                              if self.current_metrics[model_version]['confidences'] else 0.0,
                cpu_usage=cpu_usage,
                memory_usage=memory_usage
            )
            
            self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
            self._cleanup_old_metrics()
    
    def _cleanup_old_metrics(self):
        """Remove metrics older than the window size."""
        cutoff_time = datetime.now() - self.window_size
        
        # Clean history
        while self.metrics_history and self.metrics_history[0].timestamp < cutoff_time:
            self.metrics_history.popleft()
        
        # Clean current metrics
        for model_version in self.current_metrics:
            for metric_type in self.current_metrics[model_version]:
                if metric_type in ['requests', 'errors']:
                    self.current_metrics[model_version][metric_type] = [
                        ts for ts in self.current_metrics[model_version][metric_type]
                        if ts > cutoff_time
                    ]
    
    def get_current_health(self, model_version: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Get current health metrics for a model version."""
        with self.lock:
            self._cleanup_old_metrics()
            
            metrics = self.current_metrics[model_version]
            
            # Calculate metrics over the window
            request_count = len(metrics['requests'])
            error_count = len(metrics['errors'])
            error_rate = error_count / max(request_count, 1)
            
            avg_response_time = np.mean(metrics['response_times']) if metrics['response_times'] else 0.0
            avg_confidence = np.mean(metrics['confidences']) if metrics['confidences'] else 0.0
            
            # Get latest system metrics
            latest_system = None
            for metric in reversed(self.metrics_history):
                if metric.model_version == model_version:
                    latest_system = metric
                    break
            
            return {
                'request_count': request_count,
                'error_rate': error_rate,
                'avg_response_time': avg_response_time,
                'avg_confidence': avg_confidence,
                'cpu_usage': latest_system.cpu_usage if latest_system else 0.0,
                'memory_usage': latest_system.memory_usage if latest_system else 0.0,
                'requests_per_minute': request_count * (60 / self.window_size.total_seconds())
            }
    
    def compare_health(self, stable_version: str, canary_version: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Compare health metrics between stable and canary versions."""
        stable_health = self.get_current_health(stable_version)
        canary_health = self.get_current_health(canary_version)
        
        comparison = {}
        
        for metric in stable_health:
            stable_val = stable_health[metric]
            canary_val = canary_health[metric]
            
            if stable_val == 0:
                relative_change = 0.0 if canary_val == 0 else float('inf')
            else:
                relative_change = (canary_val - stable_val) / stable_val
            
            comparison[metric] = {
                'stable': stable_val,
                'canary': canary_val,
                'relative_change': relative_change,
                'absolute_change': canary_val - stable_val
            }
        
        return comparison

class TrafficController:
    """Controls traffic routing for canary deployments."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.current_split = {'stable': 100.0, 'canary': 0.0}
        self.request_count = {'stable': 0, 'canary': 0}
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    
    def set_traffic_split(self, canary_percentage: float):
        """Set traffic split percentage for canary."""
        with self.lock:
            canary_percentage = max(0.0, min(100.0, canary_percentage))
            self.current_split = {
                'stable': 100.0 - canary_percentage,
                'canary': canary_percentage
            }
            logger.info(f"Traffic split updated: {self.current_split}")
    
    def route_request(self, request_id: str) -> str:
        """Determine which model version to route request to."""
        with self.lock:
            # Use hash-based routing for consistent user experience
            import hashlib
            hash_value = int(hashlib.md5(request_id.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16)
            probability = (hash_value % 10000) / 10000.0
            
            if probability < (self.current_split['canary'] / 100.0):
                self.request_count['canary'] += 1
                return 'canary'
            else:
                self.request_count['stable'] += 1
                return 'stable'
    
    def get_traffic_stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get current traffic statistics."""
        with self.lock:
            total_requests = sum(self.request_count.values())
            
            if total_requests == 0:
                actual_split = {'stable': 0.0, 'canary': 0.0}
            else:
                actual_split = {
                    'stable': (self.request_count['stable'] / total_requests) * 100,
                    'canary': (self.request_count['canary'] / total_requests) * 100
                }
            
            return {
                'configured_split': self.current_split,
                'actual_split': actual_split,
                'request_counts': self.request_count.copy(),
                'total_requests': total_requests
            }

class CanaryDecisionEngine:
    """Makes decisions about canary deployment progression."""
    
    def __init__(self, config: CanaryConfig):
        self.config = config
        self.success_criteria = config.success_criteria or self._default_success_criteria()
        self.rollback_criteria = config.rollback_criteria or self._default_rollback_criteria()
    
    def _default_success_criteria(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Default criteria for successful canary deployment."""
        return {
            'max_error_rate_increase': 0.1,  # 10% increase in error rate
            'max_response_time_increase': 0.2,  # 20% increase in response time
            'min_confidence_threshold': 0.7,  # Minimum confidence score
            'min_requests_per_evaluation': 100  # Minimum requests before evaluation
        }
    
    def _default_rollback_criteria(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Default criteria for rolling back canary deployment."""
        return {
            'max_error_rate': 0.05,  # 5% error rate
            'max_response_time': 1000,  # 1000ms response time
            'min_confidence': 0.5,  # Minimum confidence
            'consecutive_failures': 3  # Consecutive evaluation failures
        }
    
    def evaluate_promotion(self, health_comparison: Dict[str, Any], 
                          current_traffic: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Evaluate whether to promote canary deployment."""
        decision = {
            'action': 'continue',  # continue, promote, rollback
            'new_traffic_percentage': current_traffic,
            'reasons': [],
            'metrics_passed': {},
            'metrics_failed': {}
        }
        
        # Check if we have enough requests for evaluation
        canary_requests = health_comparison.get('request_count', {}).get('canary', 0)
        if canary_requests < self.success_criteria['min_requests_per_evaluation']:
            decision['reasons'].append(
                f"Insufficient requests for evaluation ({canary_requests} < "
                f"{self.success_criteria['min_requests_per_evaluation']})"
            )
            return decision
        
        # Evaluate each metric
        passed_checks = 0
        total_checks = 0
        
        # Error rate check
        total_checks += 1
        error_rate_change = health_comparison.get('error_rate', {}).get('relative_change', 0)
        if error_rate_change <= self.success_criteria['max_error_rate_increase']:
            passed_checks += 1
            decision['metrics_passed']['error_rate'] = error_rate_change
        else:
            decision['metrics_failed']['error_rate'] = error_rate_change
            decision['reasons'].append(f"Error rate increased by {error_rate_change:.2%}")
        
        # Response time check
        total_checks += 1
        response_time_change = health_comparison.get('avg_response_time', {}).get('relative_change', 0)
        if response_time_change <= self.success_criteria['max_response_time_increase']:
            passed_checks += 1
            decision['metrics_passed']['response_time'] = response_time_change
        else:
            decision['metrics_failed']['response_time'] = response_time_change
            decision['reasons'].append(f"Response time increased by {response_time_change:.2%}")
        
        # Confidence check
        total_checks += 1
        canary_confidence = health_comparison.get('avg_confidence', {}).get('canary', 0)
        if canary_confidence >= self.success_criteria['min_confidence_threshold']:
            passed_checks += 1
            decision['metrics_passed']['confidence'] = canary_confidence
        else:
            decision['metrics_failed']['confidence'] = canary_confidence
            decision['reasons'].append(f"Confidence too low ({canary_confidence:.3f})")
        
        # Check for rollback conditions
        canary_error_rate = health_comparison.get('error_rate', {}).get('canary', 0)
        canary_response_time = health_comparison.get('avg_response_time', {}).get('canary', 0)
        
        if (canary_error_rate > self.rollback_criteria['max_error_rate'] or
            canary_response_time > self.rollback_criteria['max_response_time'] or
            canary_confidence < self.rollback_criteria['min_confidence']):
            
            decision['action'] = 'rollback'
            decision['reasons'].append("Rollback criteria triggered")
            return decision
        
        # Decide on promotion
        success_rate = passed_checks / total_checks
        
        if success_rate >= 0.8:  # 80% of checks passed
            if current_traffic >= self.config.max_traffic_percentage:
                decision['action'] = 'promote'
                decision['reasons'].append("All criteria met, promoting to stable")
            else:
                # Increase traffic
                new_traffic = min(
                    current_traffic + self.config.traffic_increment,
                    self.config.max_traffic_percentage
                )
                decision['action'] = 'continue'
                decision['new_traffic_percentage'] = new_traffic
                decision['reasons'].append(f"Criteria met, increasing traffic to {
```python
                decision['reasons'].append(f"Criteria met, increasing traffic to {new_traffic}%")
        else:
            decision['reasons'].append(f"Only {success_rate:.1%} of criteria met, maintaining current traffic")
        
        return decision

class CanaryDeployment:
    """Main canary deployment orchestrator."""
    
    def __init__(self, config: CanaryConfig, device: str = 'cpu'):
        self.config = config
        self.device = torch.device(device)
        self.status = DeploymentStatus.PREPARING
        
        # Components
        self.health_monitor = HealthMonitor()
        self.traffic_controller = TrafficController()
        self.decision_engine = CanaryDecisionEngine(config)
        
        # Models
        self.stable_model = None
        self.canary_model = None
        
        # State tracking
        self.deployment_start_time = None
        self.last_evaluation_time = None
        self.evaluation_history = []
        self.consecutive_failures = 0
        
        # Background tasks
        self.monitoring_thread = None
        self.evaluation_thread = None
        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
        
        # Database for logging
        self.db_path = f"canary_{config.deployment_id}.db"
        self._init_database()
    
    def _init_database(self):
        """Initialize database for deployment logging."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deployment_log (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    timestamp TIMESTAMP,
                    event_type TEXT,
                    model_version TEXT,
                    traffic_percentage REAL,
                    metrics TEXT,
                    decision TEXT
                )
            """)
            
            conn.execute("""
                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS request_log (
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    timestamp TIMESTAMP,
                    request_id TEXT,
                    model_version TEXT,
                    response_time REAL,
                    confidence REAL,
                    error INTEGER
                )
            """)
            conn.commit()
    
    def _load_model(self, model_path: str) -> nn.Module:
        """Load model from path."""
        if model_path.endswith('.pt') and 'traced' in model_path:
            model = torch.jit.load(model_path, map_location=self.device)
        else:
            # For demo, create a simple model
            model = self._create_demo_model()
            try:
                state_dict = torch.load(model_path, map_location=self.device)
                model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
            except:
                logger.warning(f"Could not load weights from {model_path}, using random weights")
        
        model.eval()
        model.to(self.device)
        return model
    
    def _create_demo_model(self) -> nn.Module:
        """Create demo model for testing."""
        return nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(784, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )
    
    def start_deployment(self):
        """Start the canary deployment process."""
        logger.info(f"Starting canary deployment: {self.config.name}")
        
        try:
            # Load models
            self.stable_model = self._load_model(self.config.stable_model_path)
            self.canary_model = self._load_model(self.config.canary_model_path)
            
            # Initialize traffic split
            self.traffic_controller.set_traffic_split(self.config.initial_traffic_percentage)
            
            # Update status
            self.status = DeploymentStatus.CANARY_ACTIVE
            self.deployment_start_time = datetime.now()
            self.last_evaluation_time = datetime.now()
            
            # Start background monitoring
            self._start_background_tasks()
            
            # Log deployment start
            self._log_event("deployment_started", "canary", 
                          self.config.initial_traffic_percentage, {})
            
            logger.info(f"Canary deployment started with {self.config.initial_traffic_percentage}% traffic")
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.status = DeploymentStatus.FAILED
            logger.error(f"Failed to start deployment: {e}")
            raise
    
    def _start_background_tasks(self):
        """Start background monitoring and evaluation tasks."""
        self.monitoring_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._monitoring_loop)
        self.evaluation_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._evaluation_loop)
        
        self.monitoring_thread.daemon = True
        self.evaluation_thread.daemon = True
        
        self.monitoring_thread.start()
        self.evaluation_thread.start()
    
    def _monitoring_loop(self):
        """Background loop for health monitoring."""
        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
            try:
                # Record system metrics for both models
                self.health_monitor.record_system_metrics('stable')
                self.health_monitor.record_system_metrics('canary')
                
                time.sleep(30)  # Monitor every 30 seconds
                
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Monitoring error: {e}")
    
    def _evaluation_loop(self):
        """Background loop for deployment evaluation."""
        while not self.shutdown_event.is_set():
            try:
                # Check if it's time for evaluation
                if (datetime.now() - self.last_evaluation_time).total_seconds() >= \
                   self.config.promotion_interval_minutes * 60:
                    
                    self._evaluate_deployment()
                    self.last_evaluation_time = datetime.now()
                
                time.sleep(60)  # Check every minute
                
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Evaluation error: {e}")
    
    def _evaluate_deployment(self):
        """Evaluate current deployment and make decisions."""
        if self.status != DeploymentStatus.CANARY_ACTIVE:
            return
        
        # Get health comparison
        health_comparison = self.health_monitor.compare_health('stable', 'canary')
        
        # Get current traffic
        traffic_stats = self.traffic_controller.get_traffic_stats()
        current_canary_traffic = traffic_stats['configured_split']['canary']
        
        # Make decision
        decision = self.decision_engine.evaluate_promotion(
            health_comparison, current_canary_traffic
        )
        
        # Log evaluation
        self.evaluation_history.append({
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'health_comparison': health_comparison,
            'decision': decision,
            'traffic_percentage': current_canary_traffic
        })
        
        # Execute decision
        if decision['action'] == 'promote':
            self._promote_canary()
        elif decision['action'] == 'rollback':
            self._rollback_deployment()
        elif decision['action'] == 'continue':
            new_traffic = decision['new_traffic_percentage']
            if new_traffic != current_canary_traffic:
                self.traffic_controller.set_traffic_split(new_traffic)
                self._log_event("traffic_updated", "canary", new_traffic, decision)
        
        # Track consecutive failures
        if decision['action'] == 'rollback' or len(decision['metrics_failed']) > 0:
            self.consecutive_failures += 1
        else:
            self.consecutive_failures = 0
        
        # Check for too many consecutive failures
        if self.consecutive_failures >= self.decision_engine.rollback_criteria['consecutive_failures']:
            logger.warning("Too many consecutive failures, rolling back")
            self._rollback_deployment()
        
        logger.info(f"Evaluation completed: {decision['action']} - {', '.join(decision['reasons'])}")
    
    def _promote_canary(self):
        """Promote canary to stable."""
        logger.info("Promoting canary to stable")
        
        self.status = DeploymentStatus.PROMOTING
        self.traffic_controller.set_traffic_split(100.0)  # Route all traffic to canary
        
        # In a real deployment, this would:
        # 1. Update load balancer configuration
        # 2. Replace stable model with canary model
        # 3. Update model registry
        # 4. Clean up old model
        
        self.status = DeploymentStatus.COMPLETED
        self._log_event("deployment_promoted", "canary", 100.0, {})
        
        logger.info("Canary deployment completed successfully")
    
    def _rollback_deployment(self):
        """Rollback to stable model."""
        logger.warning("Rolling back canary deployment")
        
        self.status = DeploymentStatus.ROLLING_BACK
        self.traffic_controller.set_traffic_split(0.0)  # Route all traffic to stable
        
        # In a real deployment, this would:
        # 1. Update load balancer to remove canary
        # 2. Clean up canary resources
        # 3. Alert operations team
        
        self.status = DeploymentStatus.FAILED
        self._log_event("deployment_rolled_back", "stable", 0.0, {})
        
        logger.warning("Canary deployment rolled back")
    
    def predict(self, data: np.ndarray, request_id: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Make prediction using canary deployment."""
        if self.status not in [DeploymentStatus.CANARY_ACTIVE, DeploymentStatus.PROMOTING]:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Deployment not active, status: {self.status}")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        if request_id is None:
            request_id = f"req_{int(time.time() * 1000000)}"
        
        # Route request
        model_version = self.traffic_controller.route_request(request_id)
        model = self.canary_model if model_version == 'canary' else self.stable_model
        
        try:
            # Preprocess data
            if isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
                tensor_data = torch.tensor(data, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
            else:
                tensor_data = torch.tensor(np.array(data), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
            
            if len(tensor_data.shape) == 1:
                tensor_data = tensor_data.unsqueeze(0)
            
            # Make prediction
            with torch.no_grad():
                logits = model(tensor_data)
                probabilities = torch.softmax(logits, dim=1)
                confidence, prediction = torch.max(probabilities, dim=1)
            
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Record metrics
            self.health_monitor.record_request(
                model_version, response_time, confidence.item(), error=False
            )
            
            # Log request
            self._log_request(request_id, model_version, response_time, confidence.item(), False)
            
            return {
                'prediction': prediction.item(),
                'confidence': confidence.item(),
                'model_version': model_version,
                'response_time': response_time,
                'request_id': request_id
            }
            
        except Exception as e:
            response_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Record error
            self.health_monitor.record_request(
                model_version, response_time, 0.0, error=True
            )
            
            # Log error
            self._log_request(request_id, model_version, response_time, 0.0, True)
            
            logger.error(f"Prediction error: {e}")
            raise
    
    def _log_event(self, event_type: str, model_version: str, 
                   traffic_percentage: float, data: Dict[str, Any]):
        """Log deployment event."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO deployment_log 
                (timestamp, event_type, model_version, traffic_percentage, metrics, decision)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (
                datetime.now(),
                event_type,
                model_version,
                traffic_percentage,
                json.dumps(data.get('metrics', {})),
                json.dumps(data.get('decision', {}))
            ))
            conn.commit()
    
    def _log_request(self, request_id: str, model_version: str, 
                     response_time: float, confidence: float, error: bool):
        """Log individual request."""
        with sqlite3.connect(self.db_path) as conn:
            conn.execute("""
                INSERT INTO request_log 
                (timestamp, request_id, model_version, response_time, confidence, error)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (
                datetime.now(),
                request_id,
                model_version,
                response_time,
                confidence,
                1 if error else 0
            ))
            conn.commit()
    
    def get_deployment_status(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get current deployment status."""
        traffic_stats = self.traffic_controller.get_traffic_stats()
        stable_health = self.health_monitor.get_current_health('stable')
        canary_health = self.health_monitor.get_current_health('canary')
        
        duration = None
        if self.deployment_start_time:
            duration = (datetime.now() - self.deployment_start_time).total_seconds() / 3600  # hours
        
        return {
            'deployment_id': self.config.deployment_id,
            'name': self.config.name,
            'status': self.status.value,
            'duration_hours': duration,
            'traffic_split': traffic_stats['configured_split'],
            'actual_traffic_split': traffic_stats['actual_split'],
            'total_requests': traffic_stats['total_requests'],
            'stable_health': stable_health,
            'canary_health': canary_health,
            'consecutive_failures': self.consecutive_failures,
            'last_evaluation': self.last_evaluation_time.isoformat() if self.last_evaluation_time else None
        }
    
    def get_evaluation_history(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get history of deployment evaluations."""
        return [
            {
                'timestamp': eval_data['timestamp'].isoformat(),
                'traffic_percentage': eval_data['traffic_percentage'],
                'decision': eval_data['decision'],
                'health_metrics': eval_data['health_comparison']
            }
            for eval_data in self.evaluation_history
        ]
    
    def stop_deployment(self):
        """Stop the canary deployment."""
        logger.info("Stopping canary deployment")
        
        self.shutdown_event.set()
        
        if self.monitoring_thread and self.monitoring_thread.is_alive():
            self.monitoring_thread.join(timeout=5)
        
        if self.evaluation_thread and self.evaluation_thread.is_alive():
            self.evaluation_thread.join(timeout=5)
        
        if self.status == DeploymentStatus.CANARY_ACTIVE:
            self.status = DeploymentStatus.COMPLETED
        
        self._log_event("deployment_stopped", "stable", 0.0, {})

        .status-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 20px; font-size: 0.9em; font-weight: bold; }
        .status-canary-active { background-color: #f39c12; color: white; }
        .status-promoting { background-color: #3498db; color: white; }
        .status-completed { background-color: #27ae60; color: white; }
        .status-failed { background-color: #e74c3c; color: white; }
        .metric-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; margin: 8px 0; }
        .metric-label { font-weight: bold; color: #7f8c8d; }
        .metric-value { color: #2c3e50; }
        .traffic-split { display: flex; height: 40px; border-radius: 20px; overflow: hidden; margin: 10px 0; }
        .traffic-stable { background-color: #27ae60; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: white; font-weight: bold; }
        .traffic-canary { background-color: #e74c3c; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: white; font-weight: bold; }
        .health-comparison { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 15px; margin-top: 15px; }
        .health-box { padding: 15px; border-radius: 8px; }
        .health-stable { background-color: #e8f5e8; border: 2px solid #27ae60; }
        .health-canary { background-color: #f8e8e8; border: 2px solid #e74c3c; }
        .health-title { font-weight: bold; margin-bottom: 10px; text-align: center; }
        .chart-container { background: white; padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); margin-bottom: 20px; }
        .controls { background: white; padding: 20px; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); margin-bottom: 20px; }
        .btn { padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; margin: 0 5px; }
        .btn-success { background-color: #27ae60; color: white; }
        .btn-danger { background-color: #e74c3c; color: white; }
        .btn-warning { background-color: #f39c12; color: white; }
        .btn-primary { background-color: #3498db; color: white; }
        .evaluation-log { max-height: 300px; overflow-y: auto; background-color: #f8f9fa; padding: 15px; border-radius: 8px; }
        .log-entry { margin-bottom: 10px; padding: 8px; background-color: white; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9em; }
        .log-timestamp { color: #7f8c8d; font-weight: bold; }
        .progress-bar { width: 100%; height: 20px; background-color: #ecf0f1; border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden; margin: 10px 0; }
        .progress-fill { height: 100%; background-color: #3498db; transition: width 0.3s ease; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <div class="container">
        <div class="header">
            <h1>Canary Deployment Dashboard</h1>
            <p>Real-time monitoring of canary deployment progress</p>
            <div id="deployment-info">
                <strong>Deployment:</strong> <span id="deployment-name">Loading...</span> |
                <strong>Status:</strong> <span id="deployment-status" class="status-badge">Loading...</span> |
                <strong>Duration:</strong> <span id="deployment-duration">0h</span>
            </div>
        </div>
        
        <div class="controls">
            <h3>Deployment Controls</h3>
            <button class="btn btn-success" onclick="promoteCanary()">Promote Canary</button>
            <button class="btn btn-danger" onclick="rollbackDeployment()">Rollback</button>
            <button class="btn btn-warning" onclick="pauseDeployment()">Pause</button>
            <button class="btn btn-primary" onclick="testPrediction()">Test Prediction</button>
            
            <div style="margin-top: 15px;">
                <label>Manual Traffic Split:</label>
                <input type="range" id="traffic-slider" min="0" max="100" value="5" onchange="updateTrafficSplit(this.value)">
                <span id="traffic-value">5%</span> to Canary
            </div>
        </div>
        
        <div class="status-section">
            <div class="status-card">
                <div class="status-header">Traffic Distribution</div>
                <div class="traffic-split" id="traffic-split">
                    <div class="traffic-stable" style="width: 95%;">Stable 95%</div>
                    <div class="traffic-canary" style="width: 5%;">Canary 5%</div>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Total Requests:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="total-requests">0</span>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Stable Requests:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="stable-requests">0</span>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Canary Requests:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="canary-requests">0</span>
                </div>
            </div>
            
            <div class="status-card">
                <div class="status-header">Deployment Progress</div>
                <div class="progress-bar">
                    <div class="progress-fill" id="progress-fill" style="width: 5%;"></div>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Current Stage:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="current-stage">Initial Canary</span>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Next Evaluation:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="next-evaluation">In 30 minutes</span>
                </div>
                <div class="metric-row">
                    <span class="metric-label">Consecutive Failures:</span>
                    <span class="metric-value" id="consecutive-failures">0</span>
                </div>
            </div>
            
            <div class="status-card">
                <div class="status-header">Health Overview</div>
                <div class="health-comparison">
                    <div class="health-box health-stable">
                        <div class="health-title">Stable Model</div>
                        <div>Error Rate: <span id="stable-error-rate">0.00%</span></div>
