import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

class HistogramLoggingPattern:
    """
    Pattern for detailed histogram logging and analysis
    """
    
    def __init__(self, log_dir="./logs/histograms"):
        self.writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        self.model = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(100, 256),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )
        
    def log_activation_histograms(self, x, epoch):
        """Log histograms of activations at each layer"""
        activations = {}
        
        def get_activation(name):
            def hook(model, input, output):
                activations[name] = output.detach()
            return hook
        
        # Register hooks
        hooks = []
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model):
            if isinstance(layer, (nn.Linear, nn.ReLU, nn.BatchNorm1d)):
                hook = layer.register_forward_hook(get_activation(f'layer_{i}_{layer.__class__.__name__}'))
                hooks.append(hook)
        
        # Forward pass
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = self.model(x)
        
        # Log histograms
        for name, activation in activations.items():
            self.writer.add_histogram(f'Activations/{name}', activation, epoch)
            
            # Log additional statistics
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{name}_mean', activation.mean(), epoch)
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{name}_std', activation.std(), epoch)
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{name}_sparsity', 
                                 (activation == 0).float().mean(), epoch)
        
        # Remove hooks
        for hook in hooks:
            hook.remove()
            
        return activations
    
    def log_weight_histograms(self, epoch):
        """Log detailed weight histograms"""
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                # Basic histogram
                self.writer.add_histogram(f'Weights/{name}', param, epoch)
                
                # Detailed statistics
                param_flat = param.flatten()
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Weight_Stats/{name}_mean', param_flat.mean(), epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Weight_Stats/{name}_std', param_flat.std(), epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Weight_Stats/{name}_min', param_flat.min(), epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Weight_Stats/{name}_max', param_flat.max(), epoch)
                
                # Weight magnitude distribution
                weight_magnitudes = torch.abs(param_flat)
                self.writer.add_histogram(f'Weight_Magnitudes/{name}', weight_magnitudes, epoch)
                
                # Sparsity analysis
                sparsity = (torch.abs(param_flat) < 1e-6).float().mean()
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Weight_Sparsity/{name}', sparsity, epoch)
    
    def log_gradient_histograms(self, epoch):
        """Log gradient histograms and analysis"""
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                grad = param.grad
                
                # Gradient histogram
                self.writer.add_histogram(f'Gradients/{name}', grad, epoch)
                
                # Gradient statistics
                grad_flat = grad.flatten()
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Stats/{name}_norm', torch.norm(grad), epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Stats/{name}_mean', grad_flat.mean(), epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Stats/{name}_std', grad_flat.std(), epoch)
                
                # Gradient clipping analysis
                grad_norm = torch.norm(grad)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Norms/{name}', grad_norm, epoch)
                
                # Check for vanishing/exploding gradients
                if grad_norm < 1e-7:
                    self.writer.add_scalar(f'Vanishing_Gradients/{name}', 1, epoch)
                elif grad_norm > 100:
                    self.writer.add_scalar(f'Exploding_Gradients/{name}', 1, epoch)
    
    def log_custom_distributions(self, data_dict, epoch):
        """Log custom data distributions"""
        for name, data in data_dict.items():
            if torch.is_tensor(data):
                self.writer.add_histogram(f'Custom_Distributions/{name}', data, epoch)
                
                # Percentile analysis
                percentiles = torch.quantile(data.flatten(), 
                                           torch.tensor([0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9]))
                for i, p in enumerate([10, 25, 50, 75, 90]):
                    self.writer.add_scalar(f'Percentiles/{name}_p{p}', percentiles[i], epoch)
    
    def training_with_histogram_logging(self, num_epochs=10):
        """Complete training loop with histogram logging"""
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
        
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            # Generate sample data
            x = torch.randn(64, 100)
            y = torch.randint(0, 10, (64,))
            
            # Training step
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            output = self.model(x)
            loss = criterion(output, y)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Log histograms
            self.log_activation_histograms(x, epoch)
            self.log_weight_histograms(epoch)
            self.log_gradient_histograms(epoch)
            
            # Custom distributions
            custom_data = {
                'loss_distribution': loss.repeat(100) + torch.randn(100) * 0.1,
                'prediction_confidence': torch.softmax(output, dim=1).max(dim=1)[0],
                'feature_norms': torch.norm(x, dim=1)
            }
            self.log_custom_distributions(custom_data, epoch)
            
            print(f"Epoch {epoch}: Loss = {loss.item():.4f}")
    
    def close(self):
        """Close the writer"""
        self.writer.close()

# Usage
histogram_logger = HistogramLoggingPattern()
histogram_logger.training_with_histogram_logging()
histogram_logger.close()
print("Histogram logs saved. View with: tensorboard --logdir=./logs/histograms")
```

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torchvision.transforms as transforms
from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

class ImageLoggingPattern:
    """
    Pattern for logging images, feature maps, and visualizations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, log_dir="./logs/images"):
        self.writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        self.model = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1)),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )
        
    def log_input_images(self, images, labels, epoch, num_images=8):
        """Log input images with labels"""
        # Select subset of images
        images_to_log = images[:num_images]
        labels_to_log = labels[:num_images]
        
        # Create image grid
        img_grid = torchvision.utils.make_grid(images_to_log, nrow=4, normalize=True)
        
        # Log to tensorboard
        self.writer.add_image('Input_Images', img_grid, epoch)
        
        # Log individual images with labels
        for i in range(min(num_images, 4)):
            self.writer.add_image(f'Individual_Images/class_{labels_to_log[i].item()}', 
                                images_to_log[i], epoch)
    
    def log_feature_maps(self, x, epoch, layer_idx=0):
        """Log feature maps from convolutional layers"""
        feature_maps = {}
        
        def get_features(name):
            def hook(model, input, output):
                feature_maps[name] = output
            return hook
        
        # Register hooks for conv layers
        hooks = []
        conv_idx = 0
        for i, layer in enumerate(self.model):
            if isinstance(layer, nn.Conv2d):
                hook = layer.register_forward_hook(get_features(f'conv_{conv_idx}'))
                hooks.append(hook)
                conv_idx += 1
        
        # Forward pass
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = self.model(x)
        
        # Log feature maps
        for name, features in feature_maps.items():
            # Take first sample in batch
            feature_sample = features[0]  # Shape: [channels, height, width]
            
            # Create grid of feature maps (first 16 channels)
            num_channels = min(16, feature_sample.size(0))
            feature_grid = feature_sample[:num_channels].unsqueeze(1)  # Add channel dim
            
            # Normalize for visualization
            feature_grid = (feature_grid - feature_grid.min()) / (feature_grid.max() - feature_grid.min() + 1e-8)
            
            # Create grid
            grid = torchvision.utils.make_grid(feature_grid, nrow=4, normalize=False)
            
            self.writer.add_image(f'Feature_Maps/{name}', grid, epoch)
        
        # Remove hooks
        for hook in hooks:
            hook.remove()
    
    def log_attention_maps(self, images, attention_weights, epoch):
        """Log attention visualization"""
        batch_size = min(4, images.size(0))
        
        for i in range(batch_size):
            # Original image
            orig_img = images[i]
            
            # Attention weights (assuming spatial attention)
            attention = attention_weights[i]
            
            # Resize attention to match image size
            if attention.dim() == 2:
                attention = torch.nn.functional.interpolate(
                    attention.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0),
                    size=orig_img.shape[-2:],
                    mode='bilinear'
                ).squeeze()
            
            # Create attention overlay
            attention_normalized = (attention - attention.min()) / (attention.max() - attention.min())
            
            # Convert to heatmap
            cmap = plt.cm.jet
            attention_colored = torch.tensor(cmap(attention_normalized.numpy())[..., :3])
            attention_colored = attention_colored.permute(2, 0, 1)
            
            # Overlay attention on original image
            overlay = 0.
```python
            # Overlay attention on original image
            overlay = 0.6 * orig_img + 0.4 * attention_colored
            
            self.writer.add_image(f'Attention_Maps/sample_{i}', overlay, epoch)
    
    def log_model_predictions(self, images, predictions, true_labels, epoch, num_samples=8):
        """Log images with prediction vs true label annotations"""
        batch_size = min(num_samples, images.size(0))
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(12, 6))
        axes = axes.flatten()
        
        for i in range(batch_size):
            img = images[i].permute(1, 2, 0).cpu().numpy()
            img = (img - img.min()) / (img.max() - img.min())  # Normalize
            
            pred_class = predictions[i].argmax().item()
            true_class = true_labels[i].item()
            confidence = torch.softmax(predictions[i], dim=0).max().item()
            
            axes[i].imshow(img)
            axes[i].set_title(f'True: {true_class}, Pred: {pred_class}\nConf: {confidence:.3f}')
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        self.writer.add_figure('Predictions', fig, epoch)
        plt.close(fig)
    
    def log_confusion_matrix_as_image(self, confusion_matrix, class_names, epoch):
        """Log confusion matrix as an image"""
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 8))
        
        im = ax.imshow(confusion_matrix, interpolation='nearest', cmap=plt.cm.Blues)
        ax.figure.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
        
        ax.set(xticks=np.arange(confusion_matrix.shape[1]),
               yticks=np.arange(confusion_matrix.shape[0]),
               xticklabels=class_names,
               yticklabels=class_names,
               title='Confusion Matrix',
               ylabel='True label',
               xlabel='Predicted label')
        
        # Add text annotations
        thresh = confusion_matrix.max() / 2.
        for i in range(confusion_matrix.shape[0]):
            for j in range(confusion_matrix.shape[1]):
                ax.text(j, i, format(confusion_matrix[i, j], 'd'),
                       ha="center", va="center",
                       color="white" if confusion_matrix[i, j] > thresh else "black")
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        self.writer.add_figure('Confusion_Matrix', fig, epoch)
        plt.close(fig)
    
    def log_training_progress_images(self, losses, accuracies, epoch):
        """Log training curves as images"""
        fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
        
        # Loss curve
        ax1.plot(losses)
        ax1.set_title('Training Loss')
        ax1.set_xlabel('Iteration')
        ax1.set_ylabel('Loss')
        ax1.grid(True)
        
        # Accuracy curve
        ax2.plot(accuracies)
        ax2.set_title('Training Accuracy')
        ax2.set_xlabel('Iteration')
        ax2.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
        ax2.grid(True)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        self.writer.add_figure('Training_Progress', fig, epoch)
        plt.close(fig)
    
    def close(self):
        """Close the writer"""
        self.writer.close()

# Usage example

## 214. Graph Visualization Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
import torchviz
import graphviz
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import networkx as nx

class GraphVisualizationPattern:
    """
    Pattern for visualizing model graphs and computation graphs
    """
    
    def __init__(self, log_dir="./logs/graphs"):
        self.writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        self.model = self._create_complex_model()
        
    def _create_complex_model(self):
        """Create a model with skip connections for interesting graph structure"""
        class ResidualBlock(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self, channels):
                super().__init__()
                self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1)
                self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)
                self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1)
                self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)
                
            def forward(self, x):
                residual = x
                out = torch.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
                out = self.bn2(self.conv2(out))
                out += residual
                return torch.relu(out)
        
        class ComplexModel(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 7, stride=2, padding=3)
                self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
                self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(3, stride=2, padding=1)
                
                self.res_block1 = ResidualBlock(64)
                self.res_block2 = ResidualBlock(64)
                
                self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, stride=2, padding=1)
                self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(128)
                
                self.adaptive_pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))
                self.fc = nn.Linear(128, 10)
                
            def forward(self, x):
                x = torch.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
                x = self.pool(x)
                
                x = self.res_block1(x)
                x = self.res_block2(x)
                
                x = torch.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x)))
                x = self.adaptive_pool(x)
                x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
                x = self.fc(x)
                
                return x
        
        return ComplexModel()
    
    def visualize_model_graph_tensorboard(self, input_shape=(1, 3, 224, 224)):
        """Visualize model graph in TensorBoard"""
        dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape)
        
        # Add graph to TensorBoard
        self.writer.add_graph(self.model, dummy_input)
        print("Model graph added to TensorBoard")
        
        return dummy_input
    
    def visualize_computation_graph_torchviz(self, input_tensor, save_path="computation_graph"):
        """Visualize computation graph using torchviz"""
        output = self.model(input_tensor)
        
        # Create computation graph visualization
        dot = torchviz.make_dot(output, params=dict(self.model.named_parameters()))
        
        # Customize appearance
        dot.attr(rankdir='TB')  # Top to bottom layout
        dot.attr('node', shape='box', style='rounded,filled', fillcolor='lightblue')
        
        # Save as PDF and PNG
        dot.render(save_path, format='png', cleanup=True)
        dot.render(save_path, format='pdf', cleanup=True)
        
        print(f"Computation graph saved as {save_path}.png and {save_path}.pdf")
        
        return dot
    
    def create_custom_graph_visualization(self):
        """Create custom graph visualization using networkx"""
        G = nx.DiGraph()
        
        # Add nodes for each layer
        layer_info = []
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if len(list(module.children())) == 0:  # Leaf modules
                layer_info.append({
                    'name': name,
                    'type': module.__class__.__name__,
                    'params': sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters())
                })
        
        # Add nodes to graph
        for i, info in enumerate(layer_info):
            G.add_node(i, 
                      label=f"{info['name']}\n{info['type']}\n{info['params']} params",
                      type=info['type'])
        
        # Add edges (simplified - assumes sequential flow)
        for i in range(len(layer_info) - 1):
            G.add_edge(i, i + 1)
        
        # Create visualization
        plt.figure(figsize=(15, 10))
        pos = nx.spring_layout(G, k=3, iterations=50)
        
        # Color nodes by type
        node_colors = []
        color_map = {
            'Conv2d': 'lightcoral',
            'BatchNorm2d': 'lightgreen',
            'Linear': 'lightblue',
            'ReLU': 'lightyellow',
            'MaxPool2d': 'lightpink',
            'AdaptiveAvgPool2d': 'lightgray'
        }
        
        for node in G.nodes():
            node_type = G.nodes[node]['type']
            node_colors.append(color_map.get(node_type, 'white'))
        
        # Draw graph
        nx.draw(G, pos, node_color=node_colors, node_size=2000, 
                font_size=8, font_weight='bold', arrows=True)
        
        # Add labels
        labels = {node: G.nodes[node]['label'] for node in G.nodes()}
        nx.draw_networkx_labels(G, pos, labels, font_size=6)
        
        plt.title("Model Architecture Graph", size=16)
        plt.axis('off')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig("model_architecture.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.show()
        
        return G
    
    def analyze_graph_properties(self, graph):
        """Analyze graph properties"""
        analysis = {
            'num_nodes': graph.number_of_nodes(),
            'num_edges': graph.number_of_edges(),
            'is_dag': nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(graph),
            'density': nx.density(graph),
        }
        
        if nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph(graph):
            analysis['topological_sort'] = list(nx.topological_sort(graph))
            analysis['longest_path'] = len(nx.dag_longest_path(graph))
        
        print("Graph Analysis:")
        for key, value in analysis.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        return analysis
    
    def visualize_gradient_flow(self, input_tensor):
        """Visualize gradient flow through the network"""
        input_tensor.requires_grad_(True)
        
        # Forward pass
        output = self.model(input_tensor)
        loss = output.sum()
        
        # Backward pass
        loss.backward()
        
        # Collect gradient information
        grad_info = []
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                grad_norm = param.grad.norm().item()
                grad_info.append({
                    'name': name,
                    'grad_norm': grad_norm,
                    'param_shape': list(param.shape)
                })
        
        # Create gradient flow visualization
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
        names = [info['name'] for info in grad_info]
        grad_norms = [info['grad_norm'] for info in grad_info]
        
        bars = plt.bar(range(len(names)), grad_norms)
        plt.xticks(range(len(names)), names, rotation=45, ha='right')
        plt.ylabel('Gradient Norm')
        plt.title('Gradient Flow Through Network')
        plt.yscale('log')
        
        # Color bars based on gradient magnitude
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            if grad_norms[i] < 1e-6:
                bar.set_color('red')  # Vanishing gradients
            elif grad_norms[i] > 1:
                bar.set_color('orange')  # Large gradients
            else:
                bar.set_color('green')  # Normal gradients
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig("gradient_flow.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.show()
        
        return grad_info
    
    def close(self):
        """Close the writer"""
        self.writer.close()

# Usage
graph_viz = GraphVisualizationPattern()

# Visualize model graph in TensorBoard
dummy_input = graph_viz.visualize_model_graph_tensorboard()

# Visualize computation graph with torchviz
computation_graph = graph_viz.visualize_computation_graph_torchviz(dummy_input)

# Create custom graph visualization
custom_graph = graph_viz.create_custom_graph_visualization()

# Analyze graph properties
graph_analysis = graph_viz.analyze_graph_properties(custom_graph)

# Visualize gradient flow
gradient_info = graph_viz.visualize_gradient_flow(dummy_input)

graph_viz.close()
print("Graph visualizations completed. Check TensorBoard with: tensorboard --logdir=./logs/graphs")
```

## 215. Model Inspection Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np
from collections import OrderedDict
import pandas as pd

class ModelInspectionPattern:
    """
    Comprehensive pattern for model inspection and analysis
    """
    
```python
class ModelInspectionPattern:
    """
    Comprehensive pattern for model inspection and analysis
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model):
        self.model = model
        self.model.eval()
        
    def get_model_summary(self, input_size):
        """Get comprehensive model summary"""
        summary = {
            'architecture': [],
            'total_params': 0,
            'trainable_params': 0,
            'non_trainable_params': 0,
            'total_size_mb': 0
        }
        
        # Create dummy input
        dummy_input = torch.randn(1, *input_size)
        
        # Hook to capture layer information
        layer_info = []
        
        def hook_fn(module, input, output):
            class_name = str(module.__class__).split(".")[-1].split("'")[0]
            module_idx = len(layer_info)
            
            # Input shape
            if isinstance(input, tuple):
                input_shape = [list(inp.shape) for inp in input if torch.is_tensor(inp)]
            else:
                input_shape = list(input.shape) if torch.is_tensor(input) else []
            
            # Output shape
            if isinstance(output, tuple):
                output_shape = [list(out.shape) for out in output if torch.is_tensor(out)]
            else:
                output_shape = list(output.shape) if torch.is_tensor(output) else []
            
            # Parameters
            params = sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters())
            trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
            
            layer_info.append({
                'layer_idx': module_idx,
                'layer_name': class_name,
                'input_shape': input_shape,
                'output_shape': output_shape,
                'params': params,
                'trainable_params': trainable
            })
        
        # Register hooks
        hooks = []
        for layer in self.model.modules():
            if len(list(layer.children())) == 0:  # Only leaf modules
                hook = layer.register_forward_hook(hook_fn)
                hooks.append(hook)
        
        # Forward pass
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = self.model(dummy_input)
        
        # Remove hooks
        for hook in hooks:
            hook.remove()
        
        # Compile summary
        summary['architecture'] = layer_info
        summary['total_params'] = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters())
        summary['trainable_params'] = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        summary['non_trainable_params'] = summary['total_params'] - summary['trainable_params']
        summary['total_size_mb'] = summary['total_params'] * 4 / (1024 * 1024)  # Assuming float32
        
        return summary
    
    def print_model_summary(self, input_size):
        """Print formatted model summary"""
        summary = self.get_model_summary(input_size)
        
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"{'Model Summary':^80}")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"{'Layer':<20} {'Input Shape':<25} {'Output Shape':<25} {'Params':<10}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for layer in summary['architecture']:
            input_str = str(layer['input_shape'][0] if layer['input_shape'] else "")[:24]
            output_str = str(layer['output_shape'][0] if layer['output_shape'] else "")[:24]
            
            print(f"{layer['layer_name']:<20} {input_str:<25} {output_str:<25} {layer['params']:<10,}")
        
        print("-" * 80)
        print(f"Total params: {summary['total_params']:,}")
        print(f"Trainable params: {summary['trainable_params']:,}")
        print(f"Non-trainable params: {summary['non_trainable_params']:,}")
        print(f"Model size: {summary['total_size_mb']:.2f} MB")
        print("=" * 80)
    
    def analyze_parameter_distribution(self):
        """Analyze parameter distribution across layers"""
        param_analysis = {}
        
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                param_flat = param.flatten()
                
                param_analysis[name] = {
                    'shape': list(param.shape),
                    'num_params': param.numel(),
                    'mean': param_flat.mean().item(),
                    'std': param_flat.std().item(),
                    'min': param_flat.min().item(),
                    'max': param_flat.max().item(),
                    'norm': torch.norm(param).item(),
                    'sparsity': (torch.abs(param_flat) < 1e-6).float().mean().item()
                }
        
        # Create DataFrame for better visualization
        df = pd.DataFrame(param_analysis).T
        print("\nParameter Analysis:")
        print(df.round(6))
        
        return param_analysis
    
    def inspect_layer_types(self):
        """Inspect and count different layer types"""
        layer_counts = {}
        layer_details = []
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            layer_type = module.__class__.__name__
            
            if layer_type not in layer_counts:
                layer_counts[layer_type] = 0
            layer_counts[layer_type] += 1
            
            # Get layer-specific information
            layer_info = {
                'name': name,
                'type': layer_type,
                'parameters': sum(p.numel() for p in module.parameters())
            }
            
            # Add type-specific information
            if isinstance(module, nn.Conv2d):
                layer_info.update({
                    'in_channels': module.in_channels,
                    'out_channels': module.out_channels,
                    'kernel_size': module.kernel_size,
                    'stride': module.stride,
                    'padding': module.padding
                })
            elif isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                layer_info.update({
                    'in_features': module.in_features,
                    'out_features': module.out_features,
                    'bias': module.bias is not None
                })
            elif isinstance(module, nn.BatchNorm2d):
                layer_info.update({
                    'num_features': module.num_features,
                    'eps': module.eps,
                    'momentum': module.momentum
                })
            
            layer_details.append(layer_info)
        
        print("\nLayer Type Distribution:")
        for layer_type, count in sorted(layer_counts.items()):
            print(f"  {layer_type}: {count}")
        
        return layer_counts, layer_details
    
    def check_model_health(self):
        """Check model health indicators"""
        health_report = {
            'parameter_issues': [],
            'gradient_issues': [],
            'architecture_warnings': []
        }
        
        # Check parameters
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                # Check for NaN or Inf
                if torch.isnan(param).any():
                    health_report['parameter_issues'].append(f"NaN values in {name}")
                if torch.isinf(param).any():
                    health_report['parameter_issues'].append(f"Inf values in {name}")
                
                # Check for very large or very small values
                param_abs = torch.abs(param)
                if param_abs.max() > 100:
                    health_report['parameter_issues'].append(f"Very large values in {name} (max: {param_abs.max():.2e})")
                if param_abs.min() < 1e-8 and param_abs.min() > 0:
                    health_report['parameter_issues'].append(f"Very small values in {name} (min: {param_abs.min():.2e})")
        
        # Check gradients if available
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.grad is not None:
                grad = param.grad
                if torch.isnan(grad).any():
                    health_report['gradient_issues'].append(f"NaN gradients in {name}")
                if torch.isinf(grad).any():
                    health_report['gradient_issues'].append(f"Inf gradients in {name}")
                
                grad_norm = torch.norm(grad)
                if grad_norm < 1e-8:
                    health_report['gradient_issues'].append(f"Vanishing gradients in {name} (norm: {grad_norm:.2e})")
                elif grad_norm > 100:
                    health_report['gradient_issues'].append(f"Exploding gradients in {name} (norm: {grad_norm:.2e})")
        
        # Architecture warnings
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters())
        if total_params > 100_000_000:  # 100M parameters
            health_report['architecture_warnings'].append(f"Very large model: {total_params:,} parameters")
        
        # Print health report
        print("\nModel Health Report:")
        print("-" * 40)
        
        if not any(health_report.values()):
            print("✓ Model appears healthy")
        else:
            for category, issues in health_report.items():
                if issues:
                    print(f"\n{category.replace('_', ' ').title()}:")
                    for issue in issues:
                        print(f"  ⚠ {issue}")
        
        return health_report
    
    def compare_with_reference(self, reference_model):
        """Compare current model with reference model"""
        comparison = {
            'parameter_differences': {},
            'architecture_differences': [],
            'summary_comparison': {}
        }
        
        # Compare parameters
        model_params = dict(self.model.named_parameters())
        ref_params = dict(reference_model.named_parameters())
        
        common_params = set(model_params.keys()) & set(ref_params.keys())
        
        for param_name in common_params:
            param1 = model_params[param_name]
            param2 = ref_params[param_name]
            
            if param1.shape == param2.shape:
                diff = torch.norm(param1 - param2).item()
                comparison['parameter_differences'][param_name] = {
                    'l2_difference': diff,
                    'relative_difference': diff / (torch.norm(param1).item() + 1e-8),
                    'max_absolute_diff': torch.max(torch.abs(param1 - param2)).item()
                }
            else:
                comparison['architecture_differences'].append(
                    f"Shape mismatch in {param_name}: {param1.shape} vs {param2.shape}"
                )
        
        # Parameters only in one model
        only_in_model = set(model_params.keys()) - set(ref_params.keys())
        only_in_ref = set(ref_params.keys()) - set(model_params.keys())
        
        if only_in_model:
            comparison['architecture_differences'].append(f"Parameters only in current model: {only_in_model}")
        if only_in_ref:
            comparison['architecture_differences'].append(f"Parameters only in reference model: {only_in_ref}")
        
        print("\nModel Comparison Report:")
        print("-" * 40)
        
        if comparison['parameter_differences']:
            print("Parameter Differences (top 5 by relative difference):")
            sorted_diffs = sorted(comparison['parameter_differences'].items(), 
                                key=lambda x: x[1]['relative_difference'], reverse=True)
            for name, diff in sorted_diffs[:5]:
                print(f"  {name}: rel_diff={diff['relative_difference']:.6f}, l2_diff={diff['l2_difference']:.6f}")
        
        if comparison['architecture_differences']:
            print("\nArchitecture Differences:")
            for diff in comparison['architecture_differences']:
                print(f"  {diff}")
        
        return comparison

# Usage
class SampleModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.features = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 64, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))
        )
        self.classifier = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.5),
            nn.Linear(64, 10)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.features(x)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x

# Create and inspect model
model = SampleModel()
inspector = ModelInspectionPattern(model)

# Print model summary
inspector.print_model_summary(input_size=(3, 32, 32))

# Analyze parameters
param_analysis = inspector.analyze_parameter_distribution()

# Inspect layer types
layer_counts, layer_details = inspector.inspect_layer_types()

# Check model health
health_report = inspector.check_model_health()

# Compare with reference model (same architecture but different weights)
reference_model = SampleModel()
comparison = inspector.compare_with_reference(reference_model)

## 216. Layer Activation Visualization Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
import seaborn as sns

class LayerActivationVisualizationPattern:
    """
    Pattern for visualizing and analyzing layer activations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model, log_dir="./logs/activations"):
        self.model = model
        self.model.eval()
        self.writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        self.activations = {}
        self.hooks = []
        
    def register_activation_hooks(self, layer_names=None):
        """Register hooks to capture activations"""
        def get_activation(name):
            def hook(model, input, output):
                self.activations[name] = output.detach().clone()
            return hook
        
        # Clear previous hooks
        self.clear_hooks()
        
        for name, module in self.model.named_modules():
            if layer_names is None or name in layer_names:
                if len(list(module.children())) == 0:  # Only leaf modules
                    hook = module.register_forward_hook(get_activation(name))
                    self.hooks.append(hook)
    
    def clear_hooks(self):
        """Clear all registered hooks"""
        for hook in self.hooks:
            hook.remove()
        self.hooks = []
        self.activations = {}
    
    def capture_activations(self, input_tensor):
        """Capture activations for given input"""
        with torch.no_grad():
            output = self.model(input_tensor)
        return output, self.activations.copy()
    
    def visualize_conv_activations
```python
    def visualize_conv_activations(self, layer_name, max_channels=16, figsize=(15, 10)):
        """Visualize convolutional layer activations"""
        if layer_name not in self.activations:
            print(f"Layer {layer_name} not found in activations")
            return None
        
        activation = self.activations[layer_name]
        
        # Take first sample in batch
        if activation.dim() == 4:  # Conv layer: [batch, channels, height, width]
            activation = activation[0]  # Shape: [channels, height, width]
            num_channels = min(max_channels, activation.shape[0])
            
            # Create subplot grid
            cols = 4
            rows = (num_channels + cols - 1) // cols
            
            fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=figsize)
            if rows == 1:
                axes = axes.reshape(1, -1)
            
            for i in range(num_channels):
                row, col = i // cols, i % cols
                
                # Normalize activation for visualization
                act_map = activation[i].cpu().numpy()
                act_map = (act_map - act_map.min()) / (act_map.max() - act_map.min() + 1e-8)
                
                im = axes[row, col].imshow(act_map, cmap='viridis')
                axes[row, col].set_title(f'Channel {i}')
                axes[row, col].axis('off')
                plt.colorbar(im, ax=axes[row, col], fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
            
            # Hide unused subplots
            for i in range(num_channels, rows * cols):
                row, col = i // cols, i % cols
                axes[row, col].axis('off')
            
            plt.suptitle(f'Activations: {layer_name}', fontsize=16)
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.show()
            
            return fig
        else:
            print(f"Layer {layer_name} is not a convolutional layer")
            return None
    
    def analyze_activation_statistics(self, layer_name):
        """Analyze statistical properties of activations"""
        if layer_name not in self.activations:
            print(f"Layer {layer_name} not found in activations")
            return None
        
        activation = self.activations[layer_name]
        flat_activation = activation.flatten()
        
        stats = {
            'shape': list(activation.shape),
            'mean': float(flat_activation.mean()),
            'std': float(flat_activation.std()),
            'min': float(flat_activation.min()),
            'max': float(flat_activation.max()),
            'sparsity': float((flat_activation == 0).float().mean()),
            'dead_neurons': 0,
            'saturation': 0
        }
        
        # Calculate dead neurons (for ReLU-like activations)
        if activation.dim() >= 2:
            # For conv layers, check across spatial dimensions
            if activation.dim() == 4:  # [batch, channels, height, width]
                channel_activity = activation.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3))
                stats['dead_neurons'] = float((channel_activity == 0).float().mean())
            elif activation.dim() == 2:  # [batch, features]
                neuron_activity = activation.mean(dim=0)
                stats['dead_neurons'] = float((neuron_activity == 0).float().mean())
        
        # Calculate saturation (assuming ReLU or similar)
        if stats['max'] > 0:
            high_activation = flat_activation > (stats['max'] * 0.9)
            stats['saturation'] = float(high_activation.float().mean())
        
        return stats
    
    def plot_activation_distribution(self, layer_names=None, bins=50):
        """Plot activation distributions for multiple layers"""
        if layer_names is None:
            layer_names = list(self.activations.keys())
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10))
        axes = axes.flatten()
        
        for i, layer_name in enumerate(layer_names[:4]):
            if layer_name in self.activations:
                activation = self.activations[layer_name].flatten().cpu().numpy()
                
                axes[i].hist(activation, bins=bins, alpha=0.7, density=True)
                axes[i].set_title(f'{layer_name}\nMean: {activation.mean():.3f}, Std: {activation.std():.3f}')
                axes[i].set_xlabel('Activation Value')
                axes[i].set_ylabel('Density')
                axes[i].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Hide unused subplots
        for i in range(len(layer_names), 4):
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        
        return fig
    
    def create_activation_heatmap(self, layer_names=None):
        """Create heatmap of activation statistics across layers"""
        if layer_names is None:
            layer_names = list(self.activations.keys())
        
        stats_data = []
        for layer_name in layer_names:
            stats = self.analyze_activation_statistics(layer_name)
            if stats:
                stats_data.append([
                    stats['mean'],
                    stats['std'],
                    stats['sparsity'],
                    stats['dead_neurons'],
                    stats['saturation']
                ])
        
        if not stats_data:
            print("No activation data available")
            return None
        
        # Create DataFrame for heatmap
        import pandas as pd
        df = pd.DataFrame(stats_data, 
                         columns=['Mean', 'Std', 'Sparsity', 'Dead Neurons', 'Saturation'],
                         index=layer_names)
        
        # Create heatmap
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, max(6, len(layer_names) * 0.5)))
        sns.heatmap(df, annot=True, fmt='.3f', cmap='viridis', cbar=True)
        plt.title('Activation Statistics Heatmap')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        
        return df
    
    def log_activations_to_tensorboard(self, epoch, input_tensor):
        """Log activations to TensorBoard"""
        output, activations = self.capture_activations(input_tensor)
        
        for layer_name, activation in activations.items():
            # Log activation statistics
            flat_activation = activation.flatten()
            self.writer.add_histogram(f'Activations/{layer_name}', flat_activation, epoch)
            
            # Log activation statistics as scalars
            stats = self.analyze_activation_statistics(layer_name)
            if stats:
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{layer_name}_mean', stats['mean'], epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{layer_name}_std', stats['std'], epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{layer_name}_sparsity', stats['sparsity'], epoch)
                self.writer.add_scalar(f'Activation_Stats/{layer_name}_dead_neurons', stats['dead_neurons'], epoch)
            
            # Log feature maps for conv layers
            if activation.dim() == 4 and activation.shape[1] <= 64:  # Reasonable number of channels
                # Take first sample, first few channels
                feature_maps = activation[0, :min(16, activation.shape[1])]
                
                # Normalize for visualization
                feature_maps = (feature_maps - feature_maps.min()) / (feature_maps.max() - feature_maps.min() + 1e-8)
                
                # Create grid
                import torchvision
                grid = torchvision.utils.make_grid(feature_maps.unsqueeze(1), nrow=4, normalize=False)
                self.writer.add_image(f'Feature_Maps/{layer_name}', grid, epoch)
    
    def compare_activations(self, input1, input2, layer_names=None):
        """Compare activations between two different inputs"""
        # Get activations for first input
        _, activations1 = self.capture_activations(input1)
        
        # Get activations for second input
        _, activations2 = self.capture_activations(input2)
        
        if layer_names is None:
            layer_names = list(set(activations1.keys()) & set(activations2.keys()))
        
        comparison_results = {}
        
        for layer_name in layer_names:
            if layer_name in activations1 and layer_name in activations2:
                act1 = activations1[layer_name].flatten()
                act2 = activations2[layer_name].flatten()
                
                # Calculate similarity metrics
                cosine_sim = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(act1.unsqueeze(0), act2.unsqueeze(0))
                l2_distance = torch.norm(act1 - act2)
                correlation = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([act1, act2]))[0, 1]
                
                comparison_results[layer_name] = {
                    'cosine_similarity': float(cosine_sim),
                    'l2_distance': float(l2_distance),
                    'correlation': float(correlation) if not torch.isnan(correlation) else 0.0
                }
        
        # Visualize comparison
        if comparison_results:
            metrics = ['cosine_similarity', 'l2_distance', 'correlation']
            fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5))
            
            for i, metric in enumerate(metrics):
                values = [comparison_results[layer][metric] for layer in layer_names]
                axes[i].bar(range(len(layer_names)), values)
                axes[i].set_title(f'{metric.replace("_", " ").title()}')
                axes[i].set_xticks(range(len(layer_names)))
                axes[i].set_xticklabels(layer_names, rotation=45, ha='right')
                axes[i].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
            
            plt.tight_layout()
            plt.show()
        
        return comparison_results
    
    def close(self):
        """Clean up resources"""
        self.clear_hooks()
        self.writer.close()

# Usage example
class SampleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 32, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(32)
        self.relu1 = nn.ReLU()
        self.pool1 = nn.MaxPool2d(2)
        
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
        self.relu2 = nn.ReLU()
        self.pool2 = nn.MaxPool2d(2)
        
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, 3, padding=1)
        self.relu3 = nn.ReLU()
        
        self.adaptive_pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))
        self.flatten = nn.Flatten()
        self.fc = nn.Linear(128, 10)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.pool1(self.relu1(self.bn1(self.conv1(x))))
        x = self.pool2(self.relu2(self.bn2(self.conv2(x))))
        x = self.relu3(self.conv3(x))
        x = self.adaptive_pool(x)
        x = self.flatten(x)
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x

# Create model and visualization tool
model = SampleCNN()
activation_viz = LayerActivationVisualizationPattern(model)

# Register hooks for specific layers
activation_viz.register_activation_hooks(['conv1', 'conv2', 'conv3', 'relu1', 'relu2', 'relu3'])

# Generate sample input
input_tensor = torch.randn(4, 3, 32, 32)

# Capture activations
output, activations = activation_viz.capture_activations(input_tensor)

# Visualize conv layer activations
activation_viz.visualize_conv_activations('conv1')
activation_viz.visualize_conv_activations('conv2')

# Analyze activation statistics
stats = activation_viz.analyze_activation_statistics('relu1')
print("ReLU1 Statistics:", stats)

# Plot activation distributions
activation_viz.plot_activation_distribution(['relu1', 'relu2', 'relu3'])

# Create activation heatmap
heatmap_df = activation_viz.create_activation_heatmap()

# Compare activations between different inputs
input2 = torch.randn(4, 3, 32, 32)
comparison = activation_viz.compare_activations(input_tensor, input2)

# Log to TensorBoard
activation_viz.log_activations_to_tensorboard(0, input_tensor)

activation_viz.close()
print("Activation visualization completed!")
```

This completes the comprehensive set of debugging and monitoring patterns for PyTorch. Each pattern provides specific functionality for model analysis, debugging, and visualization, helping developers understand and optimize their neural networks effectively.
## 217. Gradient Visualization Pattern

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter
import seaborn as sns

class GradientVisualizationPattern:
    """
    Pattern for visualizing and analyzing gradients throughout the network
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model, log_dir="./logs/gradients"):
        self.model = model
        self.writer = SummaryWriter(log_dir)
        self.gradient_data = {}
        self.hooks = []
        
    def register_gradient_hooks(self):
        """Register hooks to capture gradients"""
        def get_gradient_hook(name):
            def hook(grad):
                self.gradient_data[name] = grad.clone()
                return grad
            return hook
        
        # Clear previous hooks
        self.clear_hooks()
        
        for name, param in self.model.named_parameters():
            if param.requires_grad:
                hook = param.register_hook(get_gradient_hook(name))
                self.hooks.append(hook)
    
    def clear_hooks(self):
        """Clear all registered hooks"""
        for hook in self.hooks:
            hook.remove()
        self.hooks = []
        self.gradient_data = {}
    
    def compute_gradients(self, loss):
        """Compute gradients and capture them"""
        self.gradient_data = {}
        loss.backward(retain_graph=True)
        return self.gradient_data.copy()
    
    def visualize_gradient_flow(self, figsize=(15, 8)):
        """Visualize gradient flow through the network"""
        if not self.gradient_data:
            print("No gradient data available. Run compute_gradients first.")
            return None
        
        # Extract gradient norms
        layer_names = []
        grad_norms = []
        
        for name, grad in self.gradient_data.items():
            layer_names.append(name.replace('.weight', '').replace('.bias', ''))
            grad_norms.append(torch.norm(grad).item())
        
        # Create gradient flow plot
        fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=figsize)
        
        # Bar plot of gradient norms
        bars = ax1.bar(range(len(layer_names)), grad_norms)
        ax1.set_xlabel('Layer')
        ax1.set_ylabel('Gradient Norm')
        ax1.set_title('Gradient Norms Across Layers')
        ax1.set_xticks(range(len(layer_names)))
        ax1.set_xticklabels(layer_names, rotation=45, ha='right')
        ax1.set_yscale('log')
        
        # Color bars based on gradient magnitude
        norm_min, norm_max = min(grad_norms), max(grad_norms)
        for i, (bar, norm) in enumerate(zip(bars, grad_norms)):
            if norm < 1e-6:
                bar.set_color('red')  # Vanishing gradients
            elif norm > 1.0:
                bar.set_color('orange')  # Large gradients
            else:
                bar.set_color('green')  # Normal gradients
        
        # Line plot for trend analysis
        ax2.plot(range(len(layer_names)), grad_norms, 'o-', linewidth=2, markersize=6)
        ax2.set_xlabel('Layer Index')
        ax2.set_ylabel('Gradient Norm (log scale)')
        ax2.set_title('Gradient Flow Trend')
        ax2.set_yscale('log')
        ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        
        return fig
    
    def analyze_gradient_statistics(self):
        """Analyze statistical properties of gradients"""
        if not self.gradient_data:
            print("No gradient data available.")
            return None
        
        stats = {}
        
        for name, grad in self.gradient_data.items():
            flat_grad = grad.flatten()
            
            stats[name] = {
                'shape': list(grad.shape),
                'norm': float(torch.norm(grad)),
                'mean': float(flat_grad.mean()),
                'std': float(flat_grad.std()),
                'min': float(flat_grad.min()),
                'max': float(flat_grad.max()),
                'abs_mean': float(torch.abs(flat_grad).mean()),
                'sparsity': float((torch.abs(flat_grad) < 1e-8).float().mean()),
                'sign_changes': self._count_sign_changes(flat_grad)
            }
        
        return stats
    
    def _count_sign_changes(self, tensor):
        """Count sign changes in tensor (indicator of gradient noise)"""
        if tensor.numel() < 2:
            return 0
        signs = torch.sign(tensor)
        sign_changes = (signs[1:] != signs[:-1]).float().mean()
        return float(sign_changes)
    
    def create_gradient_heatmap(self, stats=None):
        """Create heatmap of gradient statistics"""
        if stats is None:
            stats = self.analyze_gradient_statistics()
        
        if not stats:
            return None
        
        # Prepare data for heatmap
        import pandas as pd
        
        metrics = ['norm', 'abs_mean', 'std', 'sparsity', 'sign_changes']
        data = []
        layer_names = []
        
        for name, stat in stats.items():
            layer_names.append(name)
            data.append([stat[metric] for metric in metrics])
        
        df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=metrics, index=layer_names)
        
        # Normalize columns for better visualization
        df_normalized = df.copy()
        for col in df.columns:
            if df[col].max() > 0:
                df_normalized[col] = (df[col] - df[col].min()) / (df[col].max() - df[col].min())
        
        # Create heatmap
        plt.figure(figsize=(10, max(6, len(layer_names) * 0.4)))
        sns.heatmap(df_normalized, annot=True, fmt='.3f', cmap='viridis', cbar=True)
        plt.title('Normalized Gradient Statistics Heatmap')
        plt.xlabel('Metrics')
        plt.ylabel('Layers')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        
        return df
    
    def detect_gradient_problems(self, threshold_vanishing=1e-6, threshold_exploding=100):
        """Detect gradient problems like vanishing/exploding gradients"""
        if not self.gradient_data:
            print("No gradient data available.")
            return None
        
        problems = {
            'vanishing': [],
            'exploding': [],
            'dead': [],
            'noisy': []
        }
        
        stats = self.analyze_gradient_statistics()
        
        for name, stat in stats.items():
            # Vanishing gradients
            if stat['norm'] < threshold_vanishing:
                problems['vanishing'].append((name, stat['norm']))
            
            # Exploding gradients
            if stat['norm'] > threshold_exploding:
                problems['exploding'].append((name, stat['norm']))
            
            # Dead gradients (all zeros)
            if stat['sparsity'] > 0.99:
                problems['dead'].append((name, stat['sparsity']))
            
            # Noisy gradients (many sign changes)
            if stat['sign_changes'] > 0.7:
                problems['noisy'].append((name, stat['sign_changes']))
        
        # Print problems
        print("Gradient Problem Detection:")
        print("-" * 40)
        
        for problem_type, issues in problems.items():
            if issues:
                print(f"\n{problem_type.title()} Gradients:")
                for name, value in issues:
                    print(f"  {name}: {value:.2e}")
            else:
                print(f"\n✓ No {problem_type} gradient issues detected")
        
        return problems
    
    def visualize_gradient_distributions(self, layer_names=None, bins=50):
        """Visualize gradient distributions for selected layers"""
        if not self.gradient_data:
            print("No gradient data available.")
            return None
        
        if layer_names is None:
            layer_names = list(self.gradient_data.keys())[:4]  # First 4 layers
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10))
        axes = axes.flatten()
        
        for i, layer_name in enumerate(layer_names[:4]):
            if layer_name in self.gradient_data:
                grad = self.gradient_data[layer_name].flatten().cpu().numpy()
                
                # Remove extreme outliers for better visualization
                percentiles = np.percentile(grad, [1, 99])
                grad_clipped = np.clip(grad, percentiles[0], percentiles[1])
                
                axes[i].hist(grad_clipped, bins=bins, alpha=0.7, density=True, edgecolor='black')
                axes[i].axvline(grad.mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'Mean: {grad.mean():.2e}')
                axes[i].axvline(0, color='black', linestyle='-', alpha=0.5, label='Zero')
                
                axes[i].set_title(f'{layer_name}\nStd: {grad.std():.2e}, Norm: {np.linalg.norm(grad):.2e}')
                axes[i].set_xlabel('Gradient Value')
                axes[i].set_ylabel('Density')
                axes[i].legend()
                axes[i].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Hide unused subplots
        for i in range(len(layer_names), 4):
            axes[i].axis('off')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()
        
        return fig
    
    def log_gradients_to_tensorboard(self, epoch):
        """Log gradients to TensorBoard"""
        if not self.gradient_data:
            print("No gradient data available.")
            return
        
        for name, grad in self.gradient_data.items():
            # Log gradient histogram
            self.writer.add_histogram(f'Gradients/{name}', grad, epoch)
            
            # Log gradient statistics
            grad_norm = torch.norm(grad)
            grad_mean = grad.mean()
            grad_std = grad.std()
            
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Norms/{name}', grad_norm, epoch)
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Means/{name}', grad_mean, epoch)
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Stds/{name}', grad_std, epoch)
            
            # Log sparsity
            sparsity = (torch.abs(grad) < 1e-8).float().mean()
            self.writer.add_scalar(f'Gradient_Sparsity/{name}', sparsity, epoch)
    
    def compare_gradient_updates(self, optimizer_state_before, optimizer_state_after):
        """Compare gradients before and after optimizer step"""
        comparison = {}
        
        for name, grad in self.gradient_data.items():
            param_name = name.replace('.grad', '')
            
            if param_name in optimizer_state_before and param_name in optimizer_state_after:
                param_before = optimizer_state_before[param_name]
                param_after = optimizer_state_after[param_name]
                
                # Calculate update magnitude
                update = param_after - param_before
                update_norm = torch.norm(update)
                param_norm = torch.norm(param_before)
                
                comparison[name] = {
                    'gradient_norm': torch.norm(grad).item(),
                    'update_norm': update_norm.item(),
                    'param_norm': param_norm.item(),
                    'relative_update': (update_norm / (param_norm + 1e-8)).item(),
                    'gradient_to_update_ratio': (torch.norm(grad) / (update_norm + 1e-8)).item()
                }
        
        return comparison
    
    def close(self):
        """Clean up resources"""
        self.clear_hooks()
        self.writer.close()

# Usage example
class SampleNetwork(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.layers = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(784, 512),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(512, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.layers(x)

# Create model and gradient visualizer
model = SampleNetwork()
grad_viz = GradientVisualizationPattern(model)

# Register gradient hooks
grad_viz.register_gradient_hooks()

# Simulate training step
x = torch.randn(32, 784)
y = torch.randint(0, 10, (32,))

output = model(x)
loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()(output, y)

# Compute and capture gradients
gradients = grad_viz.compute_gradients(loss)

# Visualize gradient flow
grad_viz.visualize_gradient_flow()

# Analyze gradient statistics
stats = grad_viz.analyze_gradient_statistics()

# Create gradient heatmap
heatmap_df = grad_viz.create_gradient_heatmap(stats)

# Detect gradient problems
problems = grad_viz.detect_gradient_problems()

# Visualize gradient distributions
grad_viz.visualize_gradient_distributions()

# Log to TensorBoard
grad_viz.log_gradients_to_tensorboard(0)

grad_viz.close()
